title.en: Volume 204 Biographies 92: Chen Jiuchou, Di Peng, Sun Jilu, Ceng Xian, Ding Rukui, Yang Shouqian, Shang Dajie, Wang Yu, Yang Xuan

sentences.zh: 陳九疇翟鵬

translations.literal: Chen Jiuchou, Di Peng
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiuchou, Di Peng

translations.literal: (Zhang Han)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zhang Han)〉

sentences.zh: 孫繼魯曾銑丁汝夔楊守謙商大節王抒楊選

translations.literal: Sun Jilu, Ceng Xian, Ding Rukui, Yang Shouqian, Shang Dajie, Wang Yu, Yang Xuan
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jilu, Ceng Xian, Ding Rukui, Yang Shouqian, Shang Dajie, Wang Yu, Yang Xuan

sentences.zh: 陳九疇，字禹學，曹州人。

translations.literal: Chen Jiuchou, style name Yuxue, was a man of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiuchou, whose style was Yuxue, came from Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 倜儻多權略。

translations.literal: He was unconventional and possessed many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Unconventional in temperament, he was full of resourceful stratagems.

sentences.zh: 自為諸生，即習武事。

translations.literal: From the time he was a student, he studied military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even while still a student, he trained in military matters.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifteenth year of the Hongzhi reign (1502).

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 有重囚越獄，人莫敢攖，九疇挺槊逐得之，遂以武健名。

translations.literal: When a serious criminal escaped from prison and no one dared intervene, Jiuchou took up a spear and pursued him until he was captured; he thereby gained renown for martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: When a dangerous prisoner broke out of jail and no one dared confront him, Jiuchou seized a spear, chased him down, and captured him—earning a reputation for martial valor.

sentences.zh: 正德初，錄囚南畿，忤劉瑾，謫陽山知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, while reviewing prisoners in the southern metropolitan region, he offended Liu Jin and was demoted to magistrate of Yangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign, while conducting a prison review in the southern capital region, he crossed Liu Jin and was banished to serve as magistrate of Yangshan.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，復故官。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's downfall, he was reinstated in his former post.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中，遷肅州兵備副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as bureau director and was transferred to vice commissioner for military preparedness at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to bureau director, then was appointed vice commissioner for frontier defense at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 總督彭澤之賂土魯番也，遣哈密都督寫亦虎仙往。

translations.literal: When the grand coordinator Peng Ze went to bribe Turfan, he sent the Hami commander-in-chief Xieyihuxian.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Peng Ze went to buy off Turfan with gifts, he dispatched Hami's commander Xieyihuxian on the mission.

sentences.zh: 九疇奮曰：「彭公受天子命，制邊疆，不能身當利害，何但模棱為！」

translations.literal: Jiuchou exclaimed fervently: "Lord Peng has received the Son of Heaven's commission to control the frontier—how can he not face profit and harm himself, and merely equivocate!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiuchou protested hotly: "Lord Peng bears the Son of Heaven's commission to govern the frontier. How can he refuse to face the stakes himself and only hedge his words!"

sentences.zh: 乃練卒伍，繕營壘，常若臨大敵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drilled the troops and repaired the ramparts, always as if facing a great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He then drilled his troops and repaired the fortifications, always behaving as though a major enemy were at hand.

sentences.zh: 寫亦虎仙果通賊。

translations.literal: Xieyihuxian did indeed collude with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyihuxian did in fact collude with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 番酋速檀滿速兒犯嘉峪關，遊擊芮寧敗死。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Sütan Mansur attacked Jiayuguan, and the raiding commander Rui Ning was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turfan leader Sütan Mansur attacked Jiayuguan, and the raiding commander Rui Ning was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 尋復遣斬巴思等以駝馬乞和，而陰遺書虎仙及其姻黨阿剌思罕兒、失拜煙答等俾內應。

translations.literal: Soon they again sent Zhanbasi and others with camels and horses to sue for peace, while secretly sending letters to Huxian and his kin allies Alasi Han'er and Shibai Yanda to arrange internal collusion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they sent Zhanbasi and others with camels and horses to sue for peace, while secretly writing to Huxian and his allies by marriage, Alasi Han'er and Shibai Yanda, to arrange an inside response.

sentences.zh: 九疇知賊計，執阿剌思罕兒及斬巴思付獄。

translations.literal: Jiuchou perceived the enemy's scheme and arrested Alasi Han'er and Zhanbasi and put them in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuchou saw through the enemy's plan and arrested Alasi Han'er and Zhanbasi, placing them in custody.

sentences.zh: 通事毛鑒等守之。

translations.literal: The interpreter Mao Jian and others were assigned to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: The interpreter Mao Jian and others were put in charge of guarding them.

sentences.zh: 鑒等故與通，欲縱去，眾番皆伺隙為變。

translations.literal: Jian and the others had formerly maintained communications and wished to release them; the various tribesmen all watched for an opening to revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and his fellows had long been in contact with the enemy and meant to let them go; tribesmen everywhere watched for a chance to rise.

sentences.zh: 九疇覺之，僇鑒等。

translations.literal: Jiuchou discovered this and executed Jian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuchou uncovered the plot and executed Jian and his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 賊失內應，遂拔帳走。

translations.literal: The enemy having lost their internal collusion, thereupon broke camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of their inside help, the raiders struck camp and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王瓊惡澤，並坐九疇失事罪，逮系法司獄。

translations.literal: The Minister of War Wang Qiong bore ill will toward Ze and implicated Jiuchou in the charge of misconduct for the affair, arresting him and imprisoning him in the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong, Minister of War, bore a grudge against Ze and had Jiuchou charged with mishandling the affair; he was arrested and held in the judicial prison.

sentences.zh: 以失拜煙答系死為罪，除其名。

translations.literal: He was condemned on the charge that Shibai Yanda had died in custody, and his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished because Shibai Yanda had died in prison, and his name was removed from the official registers.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，起故官。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor came to the throne, Jiuchou was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 俄進陜西按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 居數月，甘肅總兵官李隆嗾部卒毆殺巡撫許銘，焚其屍。

translations.literal: After several months, Li Long, the regional military commander of Gansu, incited his troops to beat to death the grand coordinator Xu Ming and burn his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months, Li Long, the regional commander in Gansu, incited his troops to beat Grand Coordinator Xu Ming to death and burn his body.

sentences.zh: 乃擢九疇右僉都御史，巡撫甘肅，按驗銘事，誅隆及亂卒首事者。

translations.literal: Jiuchou was thereupon promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Gansu; he investigated the Ming affair and executed Long and the ringleaders among the mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuchou was then promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Gansu; he investigated Xu's case and executed Long and the soldiers who had led the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 九疇抵鎮，言額軍七萬余，存者不及半，且多老弱，請令召募。

translations.literal: Upon arriving at his post, Jiuchou reported that of more than seventy thousand troops on the rolls, fewer than half remained, and most were old and weak; he requested permission to recruit replacements.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post, Jiuchou reported that of more than seventy thousand men on the rolls, fewer than half were actually present, and most of those were old or weak; he asked permission to recruit new troops.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his request.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，速檀滿速兒復以二萬余騎圍肅州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing, Sütan Mansur again besieged Suzhou with more than twenty thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing (1524), Sütan Mansur again laid siege to Suzhou with more than twenty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 九疇自甘州晝夜馳入城，射賊，賊多死。

translations.literal: Jiuchou rode day and night from Ganzhou into the city and shot at the enemy; many of the enemy died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuchou rode day and night from Ganzhou into the city, shot at the enemy, and killed many of them.

sentences.zh: 已，又出兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Afterwards he again led troops out and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops out again and drove the enemy away.

sentences.zh: 其分掠甘州者，亦為總兵官姜奭所敗。

translations.literal: Those who raided separately at Ganzhou were also defeated by the regional commander Jiang Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The raiding parties that struck at Ganzhou were also defeated by Regional Commander Jiang Shi.

sentences.zh: 論功，進副都御史，賚金幣。

translations.literal: In recognition of his merit he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and rewarded with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 九疇上言：「番賊敢入犯者，以我納其朝貢，縱商販，使得稔虛實也。

translations.literal: Jiuchou memorialized: "The reason the frontier tribes dare to invade is that we accept their tribute missions and permit merchants, allowing them to learn our strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuchou memorialized: "The frontier tribes dare to invade because we accept their tribute missions and allow their merchants, so that they come to know our strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 寫亦虎仙逆謀已露，輸貨權門，轉蒙寵幸，以犯邊之寇，為來享之賓。

translations.literal: Xieyihuxian's treasonous designs were already exposed, yet by presenting gifts to powerful families he in turn received imperial favor, so that a border raider became a guest come to enjoy our hospitality.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyihuxian's treason was already plain, yet by bribing powerful families he won favor at court, so that a border raider was treated as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 邊臣怵利害，拱手聽命，致內屬番人勾連接引，以至於今。

translations.literal: Frontier officials, intimidated by profit and harm, folded their hands and obeyed orders, until subjects under our rule among the tribes were enlisted as go-betweens and guides—and matters reached the present pass.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials, cowed by the stakes, simply bowed to orders, until tribesmen under our rule were enlisted as guides and go-betweens—and matters reached today's crisis.

sentences.zh: 今即不能如漢武興大宛之師，亦當效光武絕西域之計。

translations.literal: Even if we cannot now emulate Emperor Wu of Han and raise an expedition against Dayuan, we ought at least follow Emperor Guangwu's policy of cutting off the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we cannot now emulate Emperor Wu of Han and march against Dayuan, we should at least follow Emperor Guangwu's policy of severing ties with the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 先後入貢未歸者二百人，宜安置兩粵，其謀逆有跡者加之刑僇，則賊內無所恃，必不復有侵軼。

translations.literal: Of the more than two hundred who had come on tribute missions and had not yet returned, they should be settled in the two Guang provinces; those with clear evidence of treason should be punished by law, then the enemy would have no one within to rely on and would surely not raid again.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred tribesmen who had come on tribute missions and not yet returned home should be resettled in the two Guang provinces; those with clear evidence of treason should be punished. Then the enemy would have no supporters within and would surely not raid again.

sentences.zh: 倘更包含隱忍，恐河西十五衛所，永無息肩之期也。」

translations.literal: If we continue to indulge them and show forbearance, I fear the fifteen guards and posts of Hexi will never know a moment's respite."
translations.idiomatic: If we continue to indulge them, I fear the fifteen guards and posts of Hexi will never know a moment's peace."

sentences.zh: 事下，總制楊一清頗采其議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred downward, and the grand coordinator Yang Yiqing largely adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred down the bureaucracy, and Grand Coordinator Yang Yiqing largely adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 四年春致仕歸。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he retired and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he retired and went home.

sentences.zh: 初，土魯番敗遁，都指揮王輔言速檀滿速兒及牙木蘭俱死於炮，九疇以聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Turfan forces were defeated and fled, the commander Wang Fu reported that Sütan Mansur and Yamulan had both died from cannon fire, and Jiuchou reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Turfan army was beaten and fled, Commander Wang Fu reported that Sütan Mansur and Yamulan had both been killed by cannon fire, and Jiuchou relayed this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後二人上表求通貢，帝怪且疑。

translations.literal: Later the two men sent memorials requesting permission to send tribute missions, and the emperor was astonished and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Later the two men submitted memorials asking to resume tribute missions, and the emperor was astonished and suspicious.

sentences.zh: 而番人先在京師者為蜚語，言肅州之圍，由九疇激之，帝益信。

translations.literal: Meanwhile tribesmen already in the capital spread rumors saying that the siege of Suzhou had been provoked by Jiuchou, and the emperor believed this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile tribesmen already in the capital spread rumors that Jiuchou had provoked the siege of Suzhou, and the emperor believed them all the more.

sentences.zh: 會百戶王邦奇訐楊廷和、彭澤，詞連九疇。

translations.literal: At this time the platoon leader Wang Bangqi denounced Yang Tinghe and Peng Ze, and his words implicated Jiuchou as well.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Platoon Leader Wang Bangqi denounced Yang Tinghe and Peng Ze, and his accusations implicated Jiuchou as well.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書桂萼等欲緣九疇以傾澤，因請許通貢，而追治九疇激變狀。

translations.literal: Gui E and other officials of the Ministry of Personnel wished to use Jiuchou to bring down Ze, and therefore requested that tribute missions be permitted while pursuing Jiuchou on the charge of having provoked the uprising.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E, Minister of Personnel, and his allies wished to use Jiuchou to bring down Ze; they therefore asked that tribute be permitted while prosecuting Jiuchou for having provoked the disturbance.

sentences.zh: 大學士一清言事已前決。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing said the matter had already been decided beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing said the matter had already been settled.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen and had Jiuchou arrested and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen and had Jiuchou arrested and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書胡世寧言於朝曰：「世寧司刑而殺忠臣，寧殺世寧。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Punishments Hu Shining said at court: "If Shining administers punishments and yet kills a loyal minister, let Shining be killed instead."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Hu Shining said at court: "If Shining, as minister of punishments, must kill a loyal minister, then kill Shining instead."

sentences.zh: 乃上疏為訟冤曰：「番人變詐，妄騰謗讟，欲害我謀臣耳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial pleading Jiuchou's innocence, saying: "The tribesmen are deceitful and have wantonly spread slanders, seeking only to destroy our strategists.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial pleading Jiuchou's case: "The tribesmen are treacherous and have spread slanders, seeking only to destroy our strategists.

sentences.zh: 夫其畜謀內寇，為日已久。

translations.literal: Their scheme to raid from within had been long in the making.
translations.idiomatic: Their plot to raid from within had been long in preparation.

sentences.zh: 一旦擁兵深入，諸番約內應，非九疇先幾奮僇，且近遣屬夷卻其營帳，遠交瓦刺擾其窟巢，使彼內顧而返，則肅州孤城豈復能保？

translations.literal: Once they led their troops deep inside, the various tribes had agreed on internal collusion—had not Jiuchou first taken the initiative with spirited punishments, and in the near term sent subject tribesmen to drive off their camps, and in the far term allied with Oirat to harass their nests, forcing them to look inward and withdraw, how could the isolated city of Suzhou have been preserved?
translations.idiomatic: When they suddenly led their troops deep inside and the tribes had agreed on an inside response—had Jiuchou not acted first with bold punishments, sent subject tribesmen in the near term to drive off their camps, and in the far term allied with the Oirats to harass their strongholds, forcing them to look homeward and withdraw—how could the isolated city of Suzhou have been saved?

sentences.zh: 臣以為文臣之有勇知兵忘身殉國者，無如九疇，宜番人深忌而欲殺也。

translations.literal: In my view, among civil officials who are brave, understand warfare, and forget themselves for the state, none surpasses Jiuchou—thus the tribesmen must deeply fear him and wish him dead.
translations.idiomatic: Among civil officials who are brave, understand warfare, and give their lives for the state, none surpasses Jiuchou—the tribesmen must deeply fear him and wish him dead.

sentences.zh: 惟聽部下卒妄報，以滿速兒等為已死，則其罪有不免耳。」

translations.literal: He is guilty only in that he heedlessly believed his subordinates' false reports that Mansur and the others were already dead—that alone cannot be excused."
translations.idiomatic: His only fault is that he heedlessly believed his subordinates' false report that Mansur and the others were already dead—that charge alone cannot be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 已，法司具獄亦如世寧言。

translations.literal: Afterwards the judicial offices prepared the case in accordance with Shining's view as well.
translations.idiomatic: Later the judicial offices prepared the case in line with Shining's argument as well.

sentences.zh: 帝卒中萼等言，謫戍極邊。

translations.literal: The emperor unexpectedly took Gui and the others at their word and banished Jiuchou to the remotest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor unexpectedly took Gui and his allies at their word and banished Jiuchou to the remotest frontier.

sentences.zh: 居十年，赦還。

translations.literal: After ten years he was pardoned and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years he was pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 翟鵬，字誌南，撫寧衛人。

translations.literal: Di Peng, style name Zhinan, was a native of Funing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Di Peng, whose style was Zhinan, came from Funing Guard.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the third year of the Zhengde reign (1508).

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷員外郎中，出為衛輝知府，調開封。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice bureau director and bureau director, then went out as prefect of Weihui and was transferred to Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to bureau director, then served as prefect of Weihui and was transferred to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 擢陜西副使，進按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of Shaanxi and advanced to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner in Shaanxi and then to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 性剛介，歷官以清操聞。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and upright; throughout his offices he was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: By nature stern and upright, he was known throughout his career for integrity.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，擢右僉都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing (1528) he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 時邊政久馳，壯卒率占工匠私役中官家，守邊者並羸老不任兵。

translations.literal: At that time frontier administration had long been lax; able-bodied soldiers for the most part were registered as artisans and privately employed in eunuch households, while those who guarded the border were all weak, old, and unfit for military service.
translations.idiomatic: By then frontier administration had long grown slack: able-bodied soldiers were mostly registered as artisans and privately employed in eunuchs' households, while those left to guard the border were weak, old, and unfit for war.

sentences.zh: 又番休無期，甚者夫守墩，妻坐鋪。

translations.literal: Moreover, frontier leave had no fixed term; in extreme cases husbands guarded the beacon towers while wives manned the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier leave had no fixed end; in the worst cases husbands guarded beacon towers while wives manned the outposts.

sentences.zh: 鵬至，盡清占役，使得叠更。

translations.literal: When Peng arrived, he cleared all illegal registrations for private service and enabled troops to rotate in relays.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng arrived, he cleared all illegal private registrations and restored proper rotation of duty.

sentences.zh: 野雞臺二十余墩孤懸塞外，久棄不守，鵬盡復之。

translations.literal: More than twenty beacon towers at Yeji Terrace stood isolated beyond the frontier and had long been abandoned; Peng restored them all.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty beacon towers at Yeji Terrace stood isolated beyond the frontier and had long been abandoned; Peng restored them all.

sentences.zh: 歲大侵，請於朝以振。

translations.literal: In a year of severe famine he requested relief from the court.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck severely, he requested relief from the court.

sentences.zh: 坐寇入停俸。

translations.literal: He was penalized with suspension of salary because the enemy had entered the territory.
translations.idiomatic: He was fined by suspension of salary when the enemy raided his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 復坐劾總兵官趙瑛失事，為所訐，奪職歸。

translations.literal: He was again penalized for impeaching the regional commander Zhao Ying for misconduct and was denounced by Ying in turn; his office was taken away and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was again penalized for impeaching Regional Commander Zhao Ying over a military failure; Ying denounced him in turn, and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 二十年八月，俺答入山西內地。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twentieth year, Altan Khan entered the interior of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twentieth year (1541), Altan Khan raided deep into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 兵部請遣大臣督軍儲，因薦鵬。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War requested that a senior official be sent to supervise military supplies, and thereby recommended Peng.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War asked that a senior official be sent to supervise military supplies and recommended Peng.

sentences.zh: 乃起故官，整飭畿輔、山西、河南軍務兼督餉。

translations.literal: He was thereupon recalled to his former office to reorganize military affairs in the metropolitan region, Shanxi, and Henan, with concurrent supervision of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to his former rank to reorganize military affairs in the capital region, Shanxi, and Henan, with concurrent charge of supplies.

sentences.zh: 鵬馳至，俺答已飽去，而吉囊軍復寇汾、石諸州。

translations.literal: Peng rode there in haste; Altan had already withdrawn sated, but the armies of Jibeng again raided the prefectures of Fen and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Peng rode there at speed, but Altan had already withdrawn after sacking the region; Jibeng's forces then raided Fen and Shi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 鵬往來馳驅，不能有所挫。

translations.literal: Peng rushed back and forth but could inflict no setback on them.
translations.idiomatic: Peng rushed back and forth but could inflict no setback on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 寇退，乃召還。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew, he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders withdrew, he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，宣大總督樊繼祖罷，除鵬兵部右侍郎代之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, Fan Jizu, grand coordinator of Xuan and Da, was dismissed, and Peng was appointed Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year, Fan Jizu, Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu and Datong, was dismissed, and Peng was appointed Vice Minister of War in his place.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「將吏遇被掠人牧近塞，宜多方招徠。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "When officers encounter herders who have been raided grazing near the frontier, they should employ many means to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "When officers encounter herders who have been raided grazing near the frontier, they should use every means to win them back.

sentences.zh: 殺降邀功者，宜罪。

translations.literal: Those who kill surrendered men to claim merit should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who kill surrendered tribesmen to claim merit should be punished.

sentences.zh: 寇入，官軍遏敵雖無功，竟賴以安者，當錄。

translations.literal: When the enemy enters, if government troops block the enemy though without achievement, yet the region ultimately relies on them for safety, this should be recorded as merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy raids, officers who block the enemy though without a clear victory, yet by whose efforts the region is kept safe, should receive credit.

sentences.zh: 若賊眾我寡，奮身戰，雖有傷折、未至殘生民者，罪當原。

translations.literal: If the enemy are many and we few, yet one fights with all one's strength and though there are casualties the common people are not devastated, the offense should be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy outnumber our forces yet an officer fights with all his strength, and though there are casualties the people are not devastated, the offense should be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 於法，俘馘論功，損挫論罪。

translations.literal: By law, captives and severed heads determine merit, losses determine guilt.
translations.idiomatic: By law, merit is judged by captives and severed heads, guilt by losses suffered.

sentences.zh: 乃有摧鋒陷陣不暇斬首，而在後掩取者反積級受功，有逡巡觀望幸茍全，而力戰當先者反以損軍治罪，非戎律之平。」

translations.literal: Yet there are those who break the enemy line and have no time to take heads, while those in the rear who seize kills accumulate grades and receive merit; there are those who hesitate and watch, hoping merely to preserve themselves, while those who fight hard in the van are punished for losses—this is not the balance of military law."
translations.idiomatic: Yet men who break the enemy line have no time to take heads, while those in the rear who pick off stragglers pile up head-counts and win rewards; some hang back hoping merely to survive, while those who fight hardest in the van are punished for troop losses—this is not fair under military law."

sentences.zh: 帝皆從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 會有降人言寇且大入，鵬連乞兵餉。

translations.literal: At this time a surrendered tribesman said the enemy would soon raid in force, and Peng repeatedly requested troops and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When a surrendered tribesman reported that a major raid was imminent, Peng repeatedly requested troops and supplies.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，令革職閑住，因罷總督官不設。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered his office removed and that he live in retirement, and thereby abolished the post of grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, stripped him of office, and ordered him to live in retirement; the post of grand coordinator was abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 鵬受事僅百日而去。

translations.literal: Peng held office only a hundred days before he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Peng held office only a hundred days before he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，俺答復大入山西，縱掠太原、潞安。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year, Altan again raided deep into Shanxi, plundering freely through Taiyuan and Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year, Altan again raided deep into Shanxi, plundering Taiyuan and Lu'an at will.

sentences.zh: 兵部請復設總督，乃起鵬故官，令兼督山東、河南軍務，巡撫以下並聽節制。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War requested that the post of grand coordinator be reinstated; Peng was recalled to his former office and ordered concurrently to supervise military affairs in Shandong and Henan, with grand coordinators and those below all subject to his command.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War asked that the grand coordinator post be restored; Peng was recalled and given concurrent charge of military affairs in Shandong and Henan, with all grand coordinators and subordinates under his command.

sentences.zh: 鵬受命，寇已出塞。

translations.literal: Peng received his commission, but the enemy had already left the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Peng took up his commission, the raiders had already withdrawn beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 即馳赴朔州，請調陜西、薊、遼客兵八支，及宣、大三關主兵，兼募土著，選驍銳者十萬，統以良將，列四營，分布塞上，每營當一面。

translations.literal: He immediately rode to Shuozhou and requested that eight detachments of guest troops from Shaanxi, Ji, and Liao be transferred, together with the main forces of the three passes of Xuan and Da, and that local men also be recruited; selecting a hundred thousand of the fiercest, he would place them under able generals, array four camps distributed along the frontier, each camp facing one direction.
translations.idiomatic: He rode at once to Shuozhou and asked for eight detachments of auxiliary troops from Shaanxi, Ji, and Liao, the main garrisons of the three passes of Xuanfu and Datong, and local recruits; from these he would select a hundred thousand of the best fighters, place them under able generals in four camps spread along the frontier, each facing one direction.

sentences.zh: 寇入境，遊兵挑之，誘其追，諸營夾攻。

translations.literal: When the enemy entered the territory, light troops would provoke them and lure them in pursuit, and the various camps would attack from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy crossed the border, light troops would harass them and lure them in pursuit, and the camps would attack from both flanks.

sentences.zh: 脫不可禦，急趨關南依墻守，邀擊其困歸。

translations.literal: If they could not be withstood, one should hurry south of the passes to hold the wall, and intercept them when they were weary on the return.
translations.idiomatic: If they could not be stopped, troops should fall back south of the passes to hold the wall and strike the enemy when they were weary on the return.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 鵬乃浚壕築垣，修邊墻三百九十餘里，增新墩二百九十二，護墩堡一十四，建營舍一千五百間，得地萬四千九百余頃，募軍千五百人，人給五十畝，省倉儲無算。

translations.literal: Peng thereupon dredged moats and built ramparts, repaired more than three hundred ninety li of frontier wall, added two hundred ninety-two new beacon towers, fourteen protective tower forts, built one thousand five hundred barracks, gained fourteen thousand nine hundred-odd qing of land, recruited one thousand five hundred soldiers and gave each fifty mu, saving immeasurable amounts from the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Peng then dredged moats and built ramparts, repaired more than three hundred ninety li of frontier wall, added two hundred ninety-two new beacon towers and fourteen protective forts, built fifteen hundred barracks, reclaimed fourteen thousand nine hundred-odd qing of land, recruited fifteen hundred soldiers and gave each fifty mu, and saved incalculable amounts from the state granaries.

sentences.zh: 疏請東自平刑，西至偏關，畫地分守。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting that from Pingxing in the east to Pian Pass in the west, the territory be demarcated for divided defense.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that from Pingxing in the east to Pian Pass in the west, the frontier should be demarcated for divided defense.

sentences.zh: 增遊兵三支，分駐雁門、寧武、偏關。

translations.literal: He added three detachments of mobile troops, stationed separately at Yanmen, Ningwu, and Pian Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He added three mobile detachments, stationed at Yanmen, Ningwu, and Pian Pass.

sentences.zh: 寇攻墻，戍兵拒，遊兵出關夾攻，此守中有戰。

translations.literal: When the enemy attacked the wall, garrison troops resisted and mobile troops went out beyond the passes to attack from both sides—this is fighting within defense.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders struck the wall, garrison troops held them while mobile troops sallied beyond the passes to attack from both flanks—defense that includes counterattack.

sentences.zh: 東大同，西老營堡，因地設伏，伺寇所向。

translations.literal: East from Datong and west from Laoying Fort, ambushes were set according to the terrain to watch where the enemy would move.
translations.idiomatic: From Datong in the east to Laoying Fort in the west, ambushes were laid according to terrain to watch the enemy's movements.

sentences.zh: 又於宣、大、三關間，各設勁兵，而別選戰士六千，分兩營，遇警令總督武臣張鳳隨機策應，此戰中有守。

translations.literal: Moreover, between Xuan, Da, and the three passes he stationed crack troops in each place, and separately selected six thousand warriors divided into two camps; when alarm arose the military grand coordinator Zhang Feng was to respond as circumstances required—this is defense within fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He also stationed elite troops between Xuanfu, Datong, and the three passes, and selected six thousand warriors in two camps to respond under Military Grand Coordinator Zhang Feng when alarm arose—offense that includes holding ground.

sentences.zh: 帝從其議，且命自今遇敵，逗遛者都指揮以下即斬，總兵官以下先取死罪狀奏請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his proposals and moreover ordered that from now on when facing the enemy, those who hesitated at the rank of commander-in-chief and below were to be beheaded immediately, while regional commanders and below were first to take a written confession of capital crime and submit a memorial requesting execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan and ordered that henceforth anyone who dallied before the enemy at the rank of commander-in-chief or below was to be beheaded on the spot, while regional commanders and below must first sign a confession of capital crime and submit it for approval.

sentences.zh: 先是，鵬遣千戶火力赤率兵三百哨至豐州灘，不見寇。

translations.literal: Earlier, Peng had sent the battalion commander Huolichi leading three hundred troops on patrol to Fengzhou Beach, but they saw no enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Peng had sent Battalion Commander Huolichi with three hundred men to scout Fengzhou Beach, but they found no enemy.

sentences.zh: 復選精銳百，遠至豐州西北，遇牧馬者百余人，擊斬二十三級，奪其馬還。

translations.literal: He again selected a hundred elite troops who went far to the northwest of Fengzhou, encountered more than a hundred herders, struck and beheaded twenty-three of them, seized their horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a hundred picked men far northwest of Fengzhou, encountered more than a hundred herders, killed twenty-three, seized their horses, and returned.

sentences.zh: 未入塞，寇大至，官軍饑憊，盡棄所獲奔。

translations.literal: Before they had entered the passes, the enemy arrived in force; the government troops, hungry and exhausted, abandoned all they had seized and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before they re-entered the passes, a large enemy force arrived; the government troops, hungry and exhausted, abandoned their spoils and fled.

sentences.zh: 鵬具實陳狀。

translations.literal: Peng reported the facts in full.
translations.idiomatic: Peng reported the facts in full to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝以將士敢深入，仍行遷賞。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that the officers and soldiers had dared to penetrate deep, still proceeded with promotions and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting that the officers and men had dared to penetrate deep, still ordered promotions and rewards.

sentences.zh: 舊例，兵皆團操鎮城，聞警出戰。

translations.literal: By former practice, troops all drilled together in the garrison town and went out to fight when alarm was raised.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, troops drilled together in garrison towns and marched out only when alarm was raised.

sentences.zh: 自邊患熾，每夏秋間分駐邊堡，謂之暗伏。

translations.literal: Since frontier troubles grew fierce, each summer and autumn they were stationed separately at frontier forts, called 'hidden deployment.'
translations.idiomatic: As frontier troubles intensified, each summer and autumn troops were posted separately at frontier forts in what was called hidden deployment.

sentences.zh: 鵬請入秋悉令赴塞，畫地分守，謂之擺邊，九月中還鎮。

translations.literal: Peng requested that at the start of autumn all be ordered to the frontier, with demarcated territories for divided defense, called 'spread deployment along the border,' returning to the garrison in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Peng asked that at autumn's start all troops move to the frontier for divided deployment along the border, returning to garrison towns in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 遂著為令。

translations.literal: This was thereupon established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This was established as permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 二十三年正月，帝以去歲無寇為將帥力，降敕獎鵬，賜以襲衣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-third year, the emperor, considering that there had been no raiders the previous year through the generals' efforts, issued an edict praising Peng and bestowed court robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-third year, the emperor credited the generals for the previous year's freedom from raids, issued an edict praising Peng, and bestowed court robes.

sentences.zh: 至三月，俺答寇宣府龍門所，總兵官郤永等卻之，斬五十一級。

translations.literal: By the third month, Altan raided Longmen Post in Xuanfu; the regional commander Xi Yong and others repelled them and took fifty-one heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Altan raided Longmen Post in Xuanfu; Regional Commander Xi Yong and others drove him off and took fifty-one heads.

sentences.zh: 論功，進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In recognition of merit he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 帝倚鵬殄寇，錫命屢加，所請多從，而責效甚急。

translations.literal: The emperor relied on Peng to exterminate the raiders, bestowed favors repeatedly, granted most of his requests, yet demanded results with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relied on Peng to destroy the raiders, showered him with honors, granted most of his requests, yet demanded results with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 鵬亦竭智力，然不能呼吸應變。

translations.literal: Peng also exhausted his intelligence and strength, yet could not respond flexibly at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Peng also exhausted his wits and strength, yet could not adapt swiftly to changing circumstances.

sentences.zh: 御史曹邦輔嘗劾鵬，鵬乞罷，弗允。

translations.literal: The censor Cao Bangfu once impeached Peng; Peng requested dismissal but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cao Bangfu once impeached Peng; Peng asked to resign but was refused.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，薊州巡撫朱方請撤諸路防秋兵，兵部尚書毛伯溫因並撤宣、大、三關客兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, Zhu Fang, grand coordinator of Jizhou, requested withdrawal of autumn-defense troops on all routes; Mao Bowen, Minister of War, thereupon also withdrew the guest troops of Xuan, Da, and the three passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Grand Coordinator Zhu Fang of Jizhou asked to withdraw autumn-defense troops on all routes; Minister of War Mao Bowen also withdrew the auxiliary troops at Xuanfu, Datong, and the three passes.

sentences.zh: 俺答遂以十月初寇膳房堡。

translations.literal: Altan thereupon in early the tenth month raided Shanfang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Altan then raided Shanfang Fort in early the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 為郤永所拒，乃於萬全右衛毀墻入。

translations.literal: Repelled by Xi Yong, he thereupon broke through the wall at Wanquan Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Repelled by Xi Yong, he broke through the wall at Wanquan Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 由順聖川至蔚州，犯浮屠峪，直抵完縣，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: From Shunsheng River to Yuzhou, he violated Futuyu Valley and pressed straight to Wanzian; the capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: He marched from Shunsheng River to Yuzhou, struck Futuyu Valley, and pressed straight to Wanzian; the capital was placed under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，屢下詔責鵬。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and repeatedly issued edicts blaming Peng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and repeatedly issued edicts blaming Peng.

sentences.zh: 鵬在朔州聞警。

translations.literal: Peng was at Shuozhou when he heard the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Peng was at Shuozhou when he heard the alarm.

sentences.zh: 夜半至馬邑，調兵食，復趨渾源，遣諸將遏敵。

translations.literal: At midnight he reached Mayi, arranged troops and provisions, then hurried to Hunyuan and dispatched the generals to block the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Mayi at midnight, arranged troops and supplies, then hurried to Hunyuan and dispatched generals to block the enemy.

sentences.zh: 御史楊本深劾鵬逗遛，致賊震畿輔。

translations.literal: The censor Yang Benshen impeached Peng for hesitation, causing the enemy to shake the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Benshen impeached Peng for dallying, allowing the raiders to terrify the capital region.

sentences.zh: 兵科戴夢桂繼之。

translations.literal: Dai Menggui of the military affairs section followed with the same charge.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Menggui of the military affairs section followed with the same charge.

sentences.zh: 遂遣官械鵬，而以兵部左侍郎張漢代。

translations.literal: An official was thereupon sent to arrest Peng in bonds, and Zhang Han, Left Vice Minister of War, was appointed to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were sent to arrest Peng in bonds, and Zhang Han, Left Vice Minister of War, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 鵬至，下詔獄，坐永戍。

translations.literal: When Peng arrived, he was sent to the imperial prison and sentenced to perpetual banishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng arrived at court, he was sent to the imperial prison and sentenced to perpetual banishment.

sentences.zh: 行至河西務，為民家所窘，告鈔關主事杖之。

translations.literal: On the road at Hexiwu he was harassed by a civilian household and reported to the chief clerk of the transit tax office, who had the man beaten.
translations.idiomatic: At Hexiwu on the road he was harassed by locals and had the transit-tax clerk beat the offender.

sentences.zh: 廠衛以聞，復逮至京，卒於獄。

translations.literal: The palace agents reported this; he was again arrested and brought to the capital, and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The palace agents reported this; he was arrested again, brought to the capital, and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 人皆惜之。

translations.literal: All regretted his fate.
translations.idiomatic: All who knew of it regretted his fate.

sentences.zh: 初，鵬在衛輝，將入覲，行李蕭然，通判王江懷金遺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Peng was at Weihui about to go to court for audience, his luggage was bare; the vice prefect Wang Jiang carried gold to present to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Peng was at Weihui about to go to court, his luggage was bare; Vice Prefect Wang Jiang brought gold as a gift.

sentences.zh: 鵬曰：「豈我素履未孚於人耶？」

translations.literal: Peng said: "Has my conduct of integrity failed to win trust from others?"
translations.idiomatic: Peng said, "Have I failed to live so uprightly that others cannot trust me?"

sentences.zh: 江慚而退，其介如此。

translations.literal: Jiang withdrew in shame; such was his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang withdrew in shame. Such was his uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign his office was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 張漢，鐘祥人。

translations.literal: Zhang Han was a native of Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han came from Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 代鵬時，寇已出境，乃命翁萬達總督宣、大，而以漢專督畿輔、河南、山東諸軍。

translations.literal: When he replaced Peng, the enemy had already left the frontier; Weng Wanda was appointed grand coordinator of Xuan and Da, while Han was charged solely with supervising the armies of the metropolitan region, Henan, and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When he replaced Peng, the raiders had already withdrawn; Weng Wanda was made Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu and Datong, while Han supervised armies in the capital region, Henan, and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 漢條上選將、練兵、信賞、必罰四事，請令大將得專殺偏裨，而總督亦得斬大將，人知退怯必死，自爭赴敵。

translations.literal: Han submitted in detail four matters—selecting generals, drilling troops, trusting rewards, and certain punishments—and requested that great generals be empowered to execute staff officers on their own authority, while grand coordinators might also execute great generals, so that men knowing retreat and cowardice meant certain death would vie to advance against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Han laid out four proposals—selecting generals, drilling troops, reliable rewards, and certain punishments—and asked that senior generals be empowered to execute subordinate officers and grand coordinators to execute senior generals, so that men who knew cowardice meant death would fight eagerly.

sentences.zh: 帝不欲假臣下權，惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish to lend authority to his subjects and disliked this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish to grant such authority to his subjects and disliked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 兵部言：漢老邊事，言皆可從。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War said: Han is experienced in frontier affairs; his words may all be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War said Han was experienced in frontier affairs and his proposals should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 帝令再議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered further deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered further deliberation.

sentences.zh: 部臣乃言漢議皆當，而專殺大將，與《會典》未合。

translations.literal: The ministry officials then said Han's proposals were all appropriate, but that executing great generals on one's own authority did not accord with the Collected Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials then said Han's proposals were sound, but that executing senior generals on one's own authority did not accord with the Collected Statutes.

sentences.zh: 帝姑報可。

translations.literal: The emperor for the time being approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor provisionally approved.

sentences.zh: 會考察拾遺，言官劾漢剛愎。

translations.literal: At the time of the evaluation for retained recommendations, censorial officials impeached Han for obstinacy.
translations.idiomatic: During the evaluation for retained recommendations, censorial officials impeached Han for obstinacy.

sentences.zh: 遂械系詔獄，謫戍鎮西衛。

translations.literal: He was thereupon arrested in bonds and sent to the imperial prison, then banished to garrison duty at Zhenxi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested, sent to the imperial prison, and banished to Zhenxi Guard.

sentences.zh: 後數年邊警，御史陳九德薦漢。

translations.literal: Several years later, when frontier alarm arose, the censor Chen Jiude recommended Han.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, when frontier alarm arose, Censor Chen Jiude recommended Han.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，斥九德為民。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and dismissed Jiude to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and reduced Jiude to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 漢居戍所二十年卒。

translations.literal: Han lived at his garrison post twenty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: Han lived at his garrison post for twenty years and died there.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 孫繼魯，字道甫，雲南右衛人。

translations.literal: Sun Jilu, style name Daofu, was a native of Yunnan Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jilu, whose style was Daofu, came from Yunnan Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授澧州知州。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 坐事，改國子助教。

translations.literal: For an offense he was transferred to assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was transferred to assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部郎中，監通州倉。

translations.literal: He served as bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and supervised the Tongzhou granary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and supervised the Tongzhou granary.

sentences.zh: 歷知衛輝、淮安二府。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Weihui and Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as prefect of Weihui and Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 織造中官過淮，繼魯與之忤。

translations.literal: When a eunuch of the weaving bureau passed through Huai'an, Jilu clashed with him.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch of the weaving bureau passed through Huai'an, Jilu clashed with him.

sentences.zh: 誣逮至京，大學士夏言救免。

translations.literal: Falsely accused, he was arrested and brought to the capital; the Grand Secretary Xia Yan secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Falsely accused, he was arrested and brought to the capital; Grand Secretary Xia Yan secured his release.

sentences.zh: 繼魯不謝，言不悅。

translations.literal: Jilu did not thank him, and Yan was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu did not thank him, and Xia Yan was displeased.

sentences.zh: 改補黎平。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Liping.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Liping.

sentences.zh: 擢湖廣提學副使，進山西參政。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of education in Huguang and advanced to administration commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner of education in Huguang, then to administration commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 數繩宗藩。

translations.literal: He repeatedly prosecuted members of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly prosecuted members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 暨遷按察使，宗藩百余人擁馬發其裝，敞衣外無長物，乃載酒謝過。

translations.literal: When he was promoted to surveillance commissioner, more than a hundred clansmen on horseback opened his baggage; apart from plain clothes there was nothing of value, and they thereupon brought wine to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: When he was promoted to surveillance commissioner, more than a hundred clansmen on horseback inspected his baggage; apart from plain clothes he owned nothing of value, and they brought wine to apologize.

sentences.zh: 遷陜西右布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十六年擢右副都御史，代楊守謙巡撫山西。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and replaced Yang Shouqian as grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and replaced Yang Shouqian as Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 繼魯耿介，所至以清節聞，然好剛使氣。

translations.literal: Jilu was upright and unyielding; wherever he went he was known for integrity, yet he liked to be forceful and assert his will.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu was upright and unyielding; wherever he served he was known for integrity, yet he was forceful and quick to anger.

sentences.zh: 總督都御史翁萬達議撤山西內邊兵，並力守大同外邊，帝報可。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator and censor-in-chief Weng Wanda proposed withdrawing the inner frontier troops of Shanxi and concentrating strength to defend the outer frontier of Datong; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Weng Wanda proposed withdrawing Shanxi's inner frontier troops and concentrating strength on Datong's outer frontier; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 繼魯抗章爭，言：「紫荊、居庸、山海諸關，東枕溟渤；

translations.literal: Jilu submitted a memorial in protest, saying: "The passes of Zijing, Juyong, and Shanhai, eastward resting on the Bohai Sea—
translations.idiomatic: Jilu protested in a memorial: "The passes of Zijing, Juyong, and Shanhai rest on the Bohai Sea to the east;

sentences.zh: 雁門、寧武、偏頭諸關，西據黃河。

translations.literal: the passes of Yanmen, Ningwu, and Piantou, westward holding the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: the passes of Yanmen, Ningwu, and Piantou hold the Yellow River to the west.

sentences.zh: 天設重險，以藩衛國家，豈可聚師曠野，洞開重門以延敵？

translations.literal: Heaven has set these formidable barriers to shield the state—how can we mass troops in open country and throw wide the heavy gates to invite the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven set these formidable barriers to shield the state—how can we mass troops in open country and throw wide the gates to invite the enemy?

sentences.zh: 夫紫荊諸關之拱護京師，與雁門諸關之屏蔽全晉，一也。

translations.literal: The Zijing passes' protection of the capital and the Yanmen passes' shielding of all Jin are one and the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Zijing passes protect the capital just as the Yanmen passes shield all Shanxi—the principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 今議者不撤紫荊以並守宣府，豈可獨撤雁門以並守大同耶？

translations.literal: Those who debate today do not withdraw the Zijing troops to concentrate on defending Xuanfu—how then can we alone withdraw Yanmen to concentrate on defending Datong?
translations.idiomatic: Those debating this do not propose withdrawing Zijing troops to concentrate on Xuanfu—how then can we alone withdraw Yanmen to concentrate on Datong?

sentences.zh: 況自偏頭、寧武、雁門東抵平刑關為山西長邊，自右衛雙溝墩至東陽河、鎮口臺為大同長邊，自丫角山至雙溝百四十里為大同緊邊，自丫角山至老牛灣百四十里為山西緊邊，論長邊則大同為急，山西差緩，論緊邊則均為最急。

translations.literal: Moreover, from Piantou, Ningwu, and Yanmen east to Pingxing Pass is Shanxi's long frontier; from Shuanggou Tower at Right Guard to Dongyang River and Zhenkou Tower is Datong's long frontier; from Yajiao Mountain to Shuanggou, one hundred forty li, is Datong's critical frontier; from Yajiao Mountain to Laoniu Bay, one hundred forty li, is Shanxi's critical frontier—in terms of the long frontier Datong is urgent and Shanxi somewhat less so, but in terms of the critical frontier both are most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: From Piantou, Ningwu, and Yanmen east to Pingxing Pass is Shanxi's long frontier; from Shuanggou Tower to Dongyang River and Zhenkou Tower is Datong's long frontier; from Yajiao Mountain to Shuanggou is Datong's critical frontier, and from Yajiao Mountain to Laoniu Bay is Shanxi's critical frontier. On the long frontier Datong is the more urgent, but on the critical frontier both are equally urgent.

sentences.zh: 此皆密邇河套，譬之門闔。

translations.literal: All these lie close to the Ordos, like the leaves of a door.
translations.idiomatic: All lie close to the Ordos—they are like the leaves of a door.

sentences.zh: 山西守左，大同守右。

translations.literal: Shanxi guards the left leaf, Datong the right.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi guards the left leaf, Datong the right.

sentences.zh: 山西並力守左尚不能支，又安能分力以守大同之右？

translations.literal: If Shanxi concentrates all strength on the left and still cannot hold, how can it spare strength to guard Datong's right?
translations.idiomatic: If Shanxi cannot hold even when concentrating all strength on the left, how can it spare strength to guard Datong's right?

sentences.zh: 近年寇不敢犯山西內郡者，以三關備嚴故也。

translations.literal: In recent years the reason raiders have not dared violate Shanxi's inner prefectures is that the three passes have been strictly defended.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years raiders have not dared strike Shanxi's inner prefectures because the three passes have been strictly defended.

sentences.zh: 使三關將士遠離堡戍，欲其不侵犯難矣。

translations.literal: If the officers and soldiers of the three passes are far from their forts and beacon towers, it will be hard to keep them from invading.
translations.idiomatic: If troops of the three passes are posted far from their forts, it will be hard to prevent invasion.

sentences.zh: 全師在外，強寇內侵，即紫荊、倒馬諸關不將徒守哉！」

translations.literal: With the whole army outside, a strong enemy invades within—will not even the Zijing and Daoma passes be defended in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: With the whole army deployed outside, a strong enemy strikes within—will not even the Zijing and Daoma passes be left to empty defense!"

sentences.zh: 萬達聞之不悅，上疏言：「增兵擺邊，始於近歲，與額設守邊者不同。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda heard this with displeasure and submitted a memorial saying: "Increasing troops for spread deployment along the border began only in recent years and differs from the troops allotted for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda was displeased and memorialized: "Increasing troops for spread deployment along the border began only in recent years and differs from the allotted frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 繼魯乃以危言相恐，復遺臣書，言往歲建雲中議，宰執幾不免；

translations.literal: Jilu has used alarming words to intimidate me and again sent me a letter saying that in former years over the proposal to build Yunzhong, chief ministers nearly perished;
translations.idiomatic: Jilu has used alarming words to intimidate me and sent me a letter saying that when the Yunzhong proposal was debated years ago, chief ministers nearly perished;

sentences.zh: 近年撤各路兵，督撫業蒙罪。

translations.literal: in recent years when troops on various routes were withdrawn, grand coordinators and grand coordinators already suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: and when troops on various routes were withdrawn in recent years, grand coordinators already suffered punishment.

sentences.zh: 其詆排如此。

translations.literal: Such is his slander and exclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the tone of his attacks.

sentences.zh: 今防秋已逼，乞別調繼魯，否則早罷臣，無誤邊事。」

translations.literal: Now autumn defense presses near; I beg that Jilu be transferred elsewhere, or else dismiss me early and do not harm frontier affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Autumn defense is imminent; I beg that Jilu be transferred elsewhere, or dismiss me early rather than harm frontier affairs."

sentences.zh: 兵部是繼魯言。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War sided with Jilu's view.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War sided with Jilu.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，下廷議。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree and referred the matter to court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disagreed and referred the matter to court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請如萬達言。

translations.literal: Court officials requested that Weng Wanda's view be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials asked that Weng Wanda's view be followed.

sentences.zh: 帝方倚萬達，怒繼魯騰私書，引往事議君上。

translations.literal: The emperor was then relying on Weng Wanda and was angry that Jilu had circulated a private letter citing past events to criticize the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was relying on Weng Wanda and was angry that Jilu had circulated a private letter citing past events to criticize the throne.

sentences.zh: 而夏言亦惡繼魯，不為地，遂逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: Moreover Xia Yan also hated Jilu and gave him no support; he was thereupon arrested and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan also hated Jilu and gave him no support; Jilu was arrested and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 疽發於項，瘐死。

translations.literal: An abscess broke out on his neck and he died of wasting illness.
translations.idiomatic: An abscess broke out on his neck and he died of wasting illness in prison.

sentences.zh: 繼魯為巡撫僅四月。

translations.literal: Jilu had been grand coordinator only four months.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu had served as grand coordinator only four months.

sentences.zh: 山西人習其前政，冀有所設施，遽以非罪死，鹹為痛惜。

translations.literal: The people of Shanxi, accustomed to his earlier administration, had hoped he would accomplish something; that he suddenly died for no crime—all lamented in grief.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shanxi, accustomed to his earlier administration, had hoped he would accomplish much; that he suddenly died for no crime—all lamented in grief.

sentences.zh: 宗藩有上書訟其冤者，即前奪視其裝者也。

translations.literal: A clansman submitted a memorial pleading his innocence—this was the same one who had earlier seized and inspected his baggage.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman submitted a memorial pleading his innocence—the same man who had earlier inspected his baggage.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，贈兵部左侍郎，賜祭葬，蔭一子，謚清湣。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne, he was posthumously made Left Vice Minister of War, granted sacrificial burial, one son received hereditary privilege, and he was given the posthumous name Qingmin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Longqing Emperor ascended the throne, he was posthumously made Left Vice Minister of War, granted sacrificial burial, one son received hereditary privilege, and he was given the posthumous name Qingmin.

sentences.zh: 曾銑，字子重，江都人。

translations.literal: Ceng Xian, style name Zizhong, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Xian, whose style was Zizhong, came from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 自為諸生，以才自豪。

translations.literal: From the time he was a student he took pride in his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a student he took pride in his talent.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年成進士，授長樂知縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing he passed the civil service examination and was appointed magistrate of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of the Jiajing reign and was appointed magistrate of Changle.

sentences.zh: 征為御史，巡按遼東。

translations.literal: He was summoned as a censor and sent on inspection tour to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as censor and sent to inspect Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 遼陽兵變，執辱都御史呂經。

translations.literal: In Liaoyang the troops mutinied and seized and humiliated the censor-in-chief Lü Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At Liaoyang the troops mutinied, seizing and humiliating Censor-in-Chief Lü Jing.

sentences.zh: 銑時按金、復，急檄副總兵李監罷經苛急事，為亂軍乞赦。

translations.literal: Xian was then inspecting Jin and Fu; he urgently dispatched orders to the vice commander Li Jian to end Jing's harsh measures and pleaded for pardon for the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was then inspecting Jin and Fu prefectures; he urgently ordered Vice Commander Li Jian to end Jing's harsh policies and pleaded for pardon for the mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 經罷，趨廣寧，悍卒於蠻兒等復執辱經。

translations.literal: When Jing was dismissed, he hurried to Guangning, but the fierce soldiers Yu Man'er and others again seized and humiliated Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was dismissed, he hurried to Guangning, but fierce soldiers led by Yu Man'er again seized and humiliated him.

sentences.zh: 其月，撫順卒亦縛指揮劉雄父子。

translations.literal: That same month, soldiers at Fushun also bound Commander Liu Xiong and his son.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, soldiers at Fushun also bound Commander Liu Xiong and his son.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣侍郎林庭昂往勘，亂卒懼。

translations.literal: At this time the court sent Vice Minister Lin Ting'ang to investigate, and the mutinous soldiers were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Vice Minister Lin Ting'ang to investigate, and the mutinous soldiers grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 遼陽倡首者趙劓兒潛詣廣寧與蠻兒合謀，欲俟鎮城官拜表，集眾亂，為總兵官劉淮所覺，計不行。

translations.literal: The ringleader in Liaoyang, Zhao Jiao'er, secretly went to Guangning to conspire with Man'er, planning to wait until officials of the garrison town paid their respects at the memorial ceremony, gather the crowd, and revolt; Regional Commander Liu Huai discovered the plot and it failed.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoyang ringleader Zhao Jiao'er secretly went to Guangning to conspire with Man'er, planning to rise when garrison officials paid court respects; Regional Commander Liu Huai uncovered the plot and it failed.

sentences.zh: 復結死囚，欲俟庭昂至，閉城門為變。

translations.literal: They again allied with condemned prisoners, planning when Ting'ang arrived to shut the city gates and revolt.
translations.idiomatic: They allied again with condemned prisoners, planning to shut the city gates and revolt when Ting'ang arrived.

sentences.zh: 而銑已刺得二城及撫順為惡者姓名，密授諸將，劓兒等數十人同日捕獲。

translations.literal: But Xian had already obtained the names of evildoers in the two cities and at Fushun, secretly gave them to the generals, and Zhao Jiao'er and several dozen others were captured on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: But Xian had already obtained the names of ringleaders in both cities and at Fushun, secretly passed them to the generals, and Jiao'er and dozens of others were captured the same day.

sentences.zh: 銑上言：「往者甘肅、大同軍變，處之過輕。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized: "In former times the military mutinies in Gansu and Datong were punished too lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Xian memorialized: "When troops mutinied in Gansu and Datong in the past, punishment was too light.

sentences.zh: 群小謂辱命臣，殺主帥，罪不過此，遂相率為亂。

translations.literal: Petty men thought that insulting an imperial commissioner and killing a commander-in-chief merited no more than this, and so they followed one another into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men concluded that insulting an imperial commissioner and killing a commander merited no worse, and so they rebelled in succession.

sentences.zh: 今首惡宜急誅。」

translations.literal: Now the chief culprits should be executed at once."
translations.idiomatic: Now the chief culprits should be executed at once."

sentences.zh: 乃召還庭昂，命銑勘實，悉斬諸首惡，懸首邊城，全遼大定。

translations.literal: Ting'ang was recalled, Xian was ordered to verify the facts, all chief culprits were beheaded, their heads hung at the frontier cities, and all Liaodong was greatly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ting'ang was recalled; Xian was ordered to verify the facts; all chief culprits were beheaded and their heads hung at frontier cities, and Liaodong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 擢銑大理寺丞，遷右僉都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: Xian was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then to Right Censor-in-Chief as grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then to Right Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 俺答數入內地，銑請築臨清外城。

translations.literal: Altan repeatedly raided the interior, and Xian requested construction of the outer wall at Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: As Altan repeatedly raided inland, Xian requested construction of Linqing's outer wall.

sentences.zh: 工畢，進副都御史。

translations.literal: When the work was completed, he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was completed, he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 居三年，改撫山西。

translations.literal: After three years he was transferred to grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was transferred to Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 經歲寇不犯邊，朝廷以為功，進兵部侍郎，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: For a full year the enemy did not violate the border; the court considered this an achievement and promoted him to Vice Minister of War while retaining his post as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: For a full year the enemy did not raid the border; the court credited this achievement and promoted him to Vice Minister of War while he remained grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 二十五年夏，以原官總督陜西三邊軍務。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-fifth year, with his former rank he was made grand coordinator of the three frontiers of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Grand Coordinator of the three Shaanxi frontiers at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 寇十萬余騎由寧塞營入，大掠延安、慶陽境。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand horsemen of the enemy entered through Ningsai Camp and plundered greatly in Yan'an and Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand enemy horsemen entered through Ningsai Camp and plundered Yan'an and Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 銑率兵數千駐塞門，而遣前參將李珍搗寇巢於馬梁山陰，斬首百余級。

translations.literal: Xian led several thousand troops to hold the frontier pass while dispatching the former battalion commander Li Zhen to strike the enemy's nest on the shady slope of Mabang Mountain, taking more than a hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Xian led several thousand troops to hold the frontier pass while sending former Battalion Commander Li Zhen to strike the enemy camp on the shady slope of Mabang Mountain, taking more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 寇聞之，始遁。

translations.literal: When the enemy heard this, they began to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy heard this, they began to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 捷奏，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: A victory report was submitted and he was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Victory was reported and he was rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 既而寇屢入，遊擊高極死焉，副總兵蕭漢敗績。

translations.literal: Afterwards the enemy repeatedly entered; the raiding commander Gao Ji died, and the vice commander Xiao Han was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards the enemy raided repeatedly; Raiding Commander Gao Ji was killed and Vice Commander Xiao Han was defeated.

sentences.zh: 銑疏諸將罪，治如律。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized the generals' offenses and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Xian memorialized the generals' offenses and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 時套寇牧近塞，零騎往來，居民不敢樵采。

translations.literal: At that time Ordos raiders pastured near the frontier, and scattered horsemen came and went so that residents dared not gather firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Ordos raiders pastured near the frontier, and scattered horsemen came and went so residents dared not gather firewood.

sentences.zh: 銑方築塞，慮為所擾，乃選銳卒擊之。

translations.literal: Xian was building frontier walls and feared disturbance; he therefore selected crack troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was building frontier walls and feared disturbance; he selected crack troops to attack them.

sentences.zh: 寇稍北，間以輕騎入掠，銑復率諸軍驅之遠徙。

translations.literal: The enemy withdrew somewhat northward, but from time to time entered with light cavalry to raid; Xian again led the armies to drive them far away.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew northward but still raided with light cavalry; Xian again led the armies to drive them far away.

sentences.zh: 參將李珍及韓欽功為多，詔增銑俸一級，賜銀幣有加。

translations.literal: Battalion Commander Li Zhen and Han Qin achieved the most merit; an edict increased Xian's salary by one grade and added silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion Commander Li Zhen and Han Qin achieved the most merit; an edict increased Xian's salary one grade and added silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 銑素喜功名，又感帝知遇，益圖所報稱。

translations.literal: Xian had always delighted in achievement and fame, and feeling the emperor's favor, he strove all the more to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had always delighted in achievement, and feeling the emperor's favor, he strove all the more to repay it.

sentences.zh: 念寇居河套，久為中國患，上疏曰：「賊據河套，侵擾邊鄙將百年。

translations.literal: Reflecting that the enemy held the Ordos and had long been a calamity to China, he submitted a memorial saying: "The bandits occupy the Ordos and have harassed the frontier for nearly a century.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that the enemy held the Ordos and had long plagued China, he memorialized: "The raiders occupy the Ordos and have harassed the frontier for nearly a century.

sentences.zh: 孝宗欲復而不能，武宗欲征而不果，使吉囊據為巢穴。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong wished to recover it but could not; Emperor Wuzong wished to campaign but did not succeed, allowing Jibeng to make it his nest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong wished to recover it but could not; Emperor Wuzong wished to campaign but failed, allowing Jibeng to make it his stronghold.

sentences.zh: 出套則寇宣、大、三關，以震畿輔；

translations.literal: When they leave the Ordos they raid Xuan, Da, and the three passes, shaking the capital region;
translations.idiomatic: When they leave the Ordos they raid Xuanfu, Datong, and the three passes, shaking the capital region;

sentences.zh: 入套則寇延、寧、甘、固，以擾關中。

translations.literal: when they enter the Ordos they raid Yan, Ning, Gan, and Gu, disturbing the central region.
translations.idiomatic: when they enter the Ordos they raid Yan, Ning, Gan, and Gu, disturbing the central region.

sentences.zh: 深山大川，勢顧在敵而不在我。

translations.literal: In deep mountains and great rivers the advantage lies with the enemy and not with us.
translations.idiomatic: In deep mountains and great rivers the advantage lies with the enemy, not with us.

sentences.zh: 封疆之臣曾無有以收復為陛下言者，蓋軍興重務也；

translations.literal: Frontier officials have never spoken to Your Majesty of recovery, for military campaigns are weighty affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials have never urged recovery to Your Majesty, for military campaigns are weighty affairs;

sentences.zh: 小有挫失，媒孽踵至，鼎鑊刀鋸，面背森然。

translations.literal: a small setback brings slander in its train, and cauldrons, axes, knives, and saws stand before and behind one.
translations.idiomatic: a small setback brings slander in its train, and executioners' tools stand before and behind one.

sentences.zh: 臣非不知兵兇戰危，而枕戈汗馬，切齒痛心有日矣。

translations.literal: I am not unaware that war is perilous, yet sleeping with my weapon and sweating my horse, I have gnashed my teeth in grief for many days.
translations.idiomatic: I am not unaware that war is perilous, yet sleeping with my weapon and sweating my horse, I have gnashed my teeth in grief for many days.

sentences.zh: 竊嘗計之：秋高馬肥，弓矢勁利，彼聚而攻，我散而守，則彼勝；

translations.literal: I have considered: in autumn when horses are fat and bows and arrows are strong, if they gather to attack while we scatter to defend, they win;
translations.idiomatic: I have considered: in autumn when horses are fat and bows strong, if they gather to attack while we scatter to defend, they win;

sentences.zh: 冬深水枯，馬無宿槁，春寒陰雨，壤無燥土，彼勢漸弱，我乘其弊，則中國勝。

translations.literal: in winter when waters are deep and grasses frozen, horses have no fodder, and in spring cold rains leave no dry earth, their strength weakens and we exploit their disadvantage—then China wins.
translations.idiomatic: in winter when waters freeze and grasses wither, horses lack fodder; in spring cold rains leave no dry earth—their strength weakens and we exploit their disadvantage, then China wins.

sentences.zh: 臣請以銳卒六萬，益以山東鎗手二千，每當春夏交，攜五十日餉，水陸交進，直搗其巢。

translations.literal: I request sixty thousand crack troops, with two thousand spearmen from Shandong added; each year at the turn of spring and summer, carrying fifty days' provisions, advancing by land and water straight to their nest.
translations.idiomatic: I request sixty thousand crack troops plus two thousand Shandong spearmen; each spring and summer, carrying fifty days' provisions, advancing by land and water straight to their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 材官騶發，炮火雷激，則寇不能支。

translations.literal: When engineers deploy and cannon thunder like lightning, the enemy cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: When engineers deploy and cannon thunder like lightning, the enemy cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 此一勞永逸之策，萬世社稷所賴也。」

translations.literal: This is a policy of one effort for lasting peace, on which the dynasty for ten thousand generations depends."
translations.idiomatic: This is a policy of one effort for lasting peace, on which the dynasty for ten thousand generations depends."

sentences.zh: 遂條八議以進。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted eight proposals in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon submitted eight detailed proposals.

sentences.zh: 是時，銑與延、寧撫臣欲西自定邊營，東至黃甫川一千五百里，築邊墻禦寇，請帑金數十萬，期三年畢功。

translations.literal: At that time Xian and the grand coordinators of Yan and Ning wished to build a frontier wall from Dingbian Camp in the west to Huangfu River in the east, fifteen hundred li, to defend against the enemy, requesting several hundred thousand taels of silver to be completed in three years.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xian and the Yan and Ning grand coordinators wished to build a frontier wall from Dingbian Camp west to Huangfu River east, fifteen hundred li, requesting several hundred thousand taels to be completed in three years.

sentences.zh: 疏並下兵部。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 部臣難之，請令諸鎮文武將吏協議。

translations.literal: The ministry found it difficult and requested that military and civil officials of all garrisons deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry found it difficult and asked military and civil officials of all garrisons to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「賊據套為中國患久矣，朕宵旰念之，邊臣無分主憂者。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "The bandits' occupation of the Ordos has long been a calamity to China; I think of it day and night, yet frontier officials do not share my worry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "The enemy's occupation of the Ordos has long plagued China; I think of it day and night, yet frontier officials do not share my worry.

sentences.zh: 今銑倡恢復議甚壯，其令銑與諸鎮臣悉心上方略，予修邊費二十萬。」

translations.literal: Now Xian's proposal for recovery is very bold; let Xian and the frontier officials carefully present strategy; I grant two hundred thousand for wall repair."
translations.idiomatic: Now Xian's recovery proposal is bold; let Xian and frontier officials present strategy carefully; I grant two hundred thousand for wall repair."

sentences.zh: 銑乃益銳。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon grew all the bolder.
translations.idiomatic: Xian grew all the bolder.

sentences.zh: 而諸巡撫延綏張問行、陜西謝蘭、寧夏王邦瑞及巡按御史盛唐以為難，久不會奏。
