translations.literal: But the grand coordinators Zhang Wenxing of Yan-Sui, Xie Lan of Shaanxi, Wang Bangrui of Ningxia, and the investigating censor Sheng Tang considered it difficult and long delayed joint memorial.
translations.idiomatic: But Grand Coordinators Zhang Wenxing of Yan-Sui, Xie Lan of Shaanxi, Wang Bangrui of Ningxia, and Investigating Censor Sheng Tang considered it difficult and long delayed a joint memorial.

sentences.zh: 銑怒，疏請於帝，帝為責讓諸巡撫。

translations.literal: Xian was angry and memorialized to the emperor, who thereupon rebuked the grand coordinators.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was angry and memorialized; the emperor rebuked the grand coordinators.

sentences.zh: 會問行已罷，楊守謙代之，意與銑同。

translations.literal: Wenxing had already been dismissed and Yang Shouqian replaced him; Yang agreed with Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenxing had been dismissed and Yang Shouqian replaced him; Yang agreed with Xian.

sentences.zh: 銑遂合諸臣條上方略十八事，已，又獻營陣八圖，並優旨下廷議。

translations.literal: Xian then joined the officials in submitting eighteen strategic proposals, and afterwards presented eight camp formation diagrams; all received favorable edicts and were referred to court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then joined officials in submitting eighteen strategic proposals and eight camp formation diagrams; all received favorable edicts and court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 廷臣見上意向銑，一如銑言。

translations.literal: Court officials, seeing the emperor's inclination toward Xian, all spoke as Xian did.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials, seeing the emperor favored Xian, all spoke as Xian did.

sentences.zh: 帝忽出手詔諭輔臣曰：「今逐套賊，師果有名否？

translations.literal: The emperor suddenly issued a handwritten edict to the chief ministers saying: "In driving the Ordos bandits out now, is the army truly famous?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suddenly issued a handwritten edict to chief ministers: "In driving the Ordos enemy out now, is the army truly renowned?

sentences.zh: 兵食果有余？

translations.literal: Are provisions truly sufficient?
translations.idiomatic: Are provisions truly sufficient?

sentences.zh: 成功可必否？

translations.literal: Is success truly certain?
translations.idiomatic: Is success truly certain?

sentences.zh: 一銑何足言，如先民荼毒何？」

translations.literal: What is one Xian worth speaking of—what of the people's suffering?
translations.idiomatic: What is one Xian worth—what of the people's suffering?

sentences.zh: 初，銑建議時，輔臣夏言欲倚以成大功，主之甚力。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xian first proposed, Chief Minister Xia Yan wished to rely on him for a great achievement and supported him vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xian first proposed, Grand Secretary Xia Yan wished to rely on him for a great achievement and supported him vigorously.

sentences.zh: 及是，大駭，請帝自裁斷。

translations.literal: At this he was greatly alarmed and requested that the emperor decide for himself.
translations.idiomatic: At this he was greatly alarmed and asked the emperor to decide himself.

sentences.zh: 帝命刊手詔，遍給與議諸臣。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the handwritten edict published and distributed to all deliberating officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the handwritten edict published and given to all deliberating officials.

sentences.zh: 時嚴嵩方與言有隙，欲因以傾言，乃極言套必不可復。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Song was at odds with Yan and wished to use this to bring Yan down; he therefore argued that the Ordos could absolutely not be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song was at odds with Xia Yan and wished to bring him down; he argued the Ordos absolutely could not be recovered.

sentences.zh: 陰詆言，故引罪乞罷，以激帝怒。

translations.literal: He secretly slandered Yan and deliberately cited his own offenses to beg dismissal, so as to provoke the emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly slandered Yan and deliberately begged dismissal citing his own offenses to provoke the emperor's anger.

sentences.zh: 旋復顯攻言，謂「向擬旨褒銑，臣皆不預聞。」

translations.literal: Soon he openly attacked Yan, saying, "When the edict praising Xian was drafted, I was not consulted."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he openly attacked Yan, saying, "When the edict praising Xian was drafted, I was not consulted."

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王以旗會廷臣覆奏，遂盡反前說，言套不可復。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Yiqi joined court officials in memorializing in reply and thereupon completely reversed their former view, saying the Ordos could not be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Yiqi joined court officials in reply and completely reversed their former view, saying the Ordos could not be recovered.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣官逮銑、出以旗代之；

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon sent officials to arrest Xian and replaced him with Yiqi;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent officials to arrest Xian and replaced him with Yiqi;

sentences.zh: 責科道官不言，悉杖於廷，停俸四月。

translations.literal: he blamed the censorial officials for not speaking out, had them all beaten at court, and suspended salary four months.
translations.idiomatic: he blamed censorial officials for not speaking out, had them beaten at court, and suspended salary four months.

sentences.zh: 帝雖怒銑，然無意殺之也。

translations.literal: Although the emperor was angry with Xian, he had no intention of killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Although angry with Xian, the emperor had no intention of killing him.

sentences.zh: 鹹寧侯仇鸞鎮甘肅時，以阻撓為銑所劾，逮問。

translations.literal: Marquis Qiu Luan of Xianning, when commanding Gansu, had been impeached by Xian for obstruction and was arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Qiu Luan of Xianning, when commanding Gansu, had been impeached by Xian for obstruction and arrested for trial.

sentences.zh: 嵩故雅親鸞。

translations.literal: Song had long been on intimate terms with Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Song had long been intimate with Luan.

sentences.zh: 知銑所善同邑蘇綱者，言繼妻父，綱與銑、言嘗交關傳語，乃代鸞獄中草疏，誣銑掩敗不奏，克軍餉鉅萬，遣子淳屬所親蘇綱賂當途。

translations.literal: Knowing that Su Gang of the same district as Xian was Yan's former father-in-law and that Gang, Xian, and Yan had exchanged messages, he drafted a memorial in prison on Luan's behalf accusing Xian of concealing defeats and not reporting them, embezzling vast military provisions, and sending his son Chun through Gang to bribe those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Su Gang of Xian's district was Xia Yan's former father-in-law and that Gang, Xian, and Yan had exchanged messages, he drafted a prison memorial for Luan accusing Xian of concealing defeats, embezzling vast provisions, and sending his son Chun through Gang to bribe those in power.

sentences.zh: 其言絕無左驗，而帝深入其說，立下淳、綱詔獄。

translations.literal: There was absolutely no corroborating evidence, yet the emperor deeply believed it and sent Chun and Gang to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: There was no corroborating evidence, yet the emperor deeply believed it and sent Chun and Gang to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 給事中齊譽等見帝怒銑甚，請早正刑章。

translations.literal: Seeing the emperor's great anger at Xian, Supervising Secretary Qi Yu and others requested early application of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's great anger, Supervising Secretary Qi Yu and others requested early punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝責譽黨奸避事，鐫級調外任。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed Yu for factionalism and avoiding duty, reduced his rank, and transferred him to an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Yu for factionalism and avoiding duty, reduced his rank, and transferred him outside.

sentences.zh: 及銑至，法司比擬邊帥失陷城砦者律。

translations.literal: When Xian arrived, the judicial offices compared his case to the statute for frontier commanders who lost cities and forts.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian arrived, the judicial offices compared his case to the statute for frontier commanders who lost cities and forts.

sentences.zh: 帝必欲依正條，當銑交結近侍律斬，妻子流二千里，即日行刑。

translations.literal: The emperor insisted on applying the proper article, sentencing Xian under the statute for associating with palace attendants to execution, his wife and children exiled two thousand li, executed that very day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor insisted on the proper article, sentencing Xian under associating with palace attendants to execution, wife and children exiled two thousand li, executed that day.

sentences.zh: 銑既死，言亦坐斬，而鸞出獄。

translations.literal: After Xian died, Yan was also executed, and Luan was released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: After Xian died, Xia Yan was also executed, and Luan was released.

sentences.zh: 銑有膽略，長於用兵。

translations.literal: Xian had courage and stratagem and excelled in military use.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had courage and stratagem and excelled in warfare.

sentences.zh: 歲除夜，猝命諸將出。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve he suddenly ordered the generals out.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve he suddenly ordered the generals out.

sentences.zh: 時塞上無警，諸將方置酒，不欲行，賂鈴卒求緩於銑妾。

translations.literal: At that time there was no alarm on the frontier; the generals were setting out wine and did not wish to go, bribing the bell-ringer to ask his concubine to plead for delay with Xian.
translations.idiomatic: There was no frontier alarm; the generals were feasting and did not wish to go, bribing the bell-ringer to ask his concubine to plead for delay.

sentences.zh: 銑斬鈴卒以徇。

translations.literal: Xian executed the bell-ringer as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Xian executed the bell-ringer as an example.

sentences.zh: 諸將不得已，丙夜被甲行。

translations.literal: The generals had no choice but to don armor in the third watch and march.
translations.idiomatic: The generals had no choice but to don armor at the third watch and march.

sentences.zh: 果遇寇，擊敗之。

translations.literal: They indeed encountered the enemy and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: They indeed encountered the enemy and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 翼日入賀畢，前請故。

translations.literal: The next day after congratulations were finished, they asked the reason beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The next day after New Year congratulations they asked how he had known.

sentences.zh: 銑笑曰：「見烏鵲非時噪，故知之耳。」

translations.literal: Xian smiled and said, "I saw crows and magpies crying out of season, and so knew."
translations.idiomatic: Xian smiled and said, "I saw crows and magpies crying out of season, and so knew."

sentences.zh: 皆大服。

translations.literal: All were greatly impressed.
translations.idiomatic: All were greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 銑廉，既歿，家無余貲。

translations.literal: Xian was incorrupt; after his death his family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was incorrupt; after his death his family had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，給事中辛自修、御史王好問訟銑誌在立功，身罹重辟，識與不識，痛悼至今。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, Supervising Secretary Xin Zixiu and Censor Wang Haowen pleaded that Xian's aim had been to achieve merit and he had suffered the heavy penalty; known and unknown alike grieve to this day.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing, Supervising Secretary Xin Zixiu and Censor Wang Haowen pleaded that Xian aimed to achieve merit and suffered the heavy penalty; all grieve to this day.

sentences.zh: 詔贈兵部尚書，謚襄湣。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Minister of War with the posthumous name Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Minister of War with the posthumous name Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，從御史周磐請，建祠陜西。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, following Censor Zhou Pan's request, a shrine was built in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign, following Censor Zhou Pan's request, a shrine was built in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 李珍者，故坐事失官。

translations.literal: Li Zhen had formerly lost office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen had formerly lost office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 銑從徒中錄用，復積戰功至參將。

translations.literal: Xian selected him from among convicts, restored him, and he accumulated battle achievements until he became a battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xian selected him from convicts, restored him, and he rose through battle achievements to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 銑既被誣，詔遣給事中申價等往核，因並劾珍與指揮田世威、郭震為銑爪牙，下之詔獄。

translations.literal: After Xian was falsely accused, an edict sent Supervising Secretary Shen Jia and others to verify; they also impeached Zhen together with commanders Tian Shiwei and Guo Zhen as Xian's henchmen and sent them to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: After Xian was falsely accused, an edict sent Supervising Secretary Shen Jia to verify; Zhen was impeached with commanders Tian Shiwei and Guo Zhen as Xian's henchmen and sent to prison.

sentences.zh: 連及巡撫謝蘭、張問行，御史盛唐，副總兵李琦等，皆斥罰。

translations.literal: This implicated Grand Coordinators Xie Lan and Zhang Wenxing, Censor Sheng Tang, Vice Commander Li Qi, and others, all of whom were punished.
translations.idiomatic: This implicated Grand Coordinators Xie Lan and Zhang Wenxing, Censor Sheng Tang, Vice Commander Li Qi, and others, all punished.

sentences.zh: 勒淳、綱贓，恤陣亡軍及居民被難者。

translations.literal: Chun and Gang were forced to repay embezzled funds and compensation was given to soldiers killed in battle and residents who suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Gang were forced to repay embezzled funds; compensation was given to soldiers killed and residents who suffered.

sentences.zh: 銑嘗檄府衛銀三萬兩制車仗，亦責償於淳。

translations.literal: Xian had once requisitioned thirty thousand taels of silver from prefectures and guards for chariots and equipment, which was also charged to Chun for repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had requisitioned thirty thousand taels from prefectures and guards for equipment, also charged to Chun.

sentences.zh: 且酷刑拷珍，令其實克餉行賂事，幾死，卒不承。

translations.literal: He also tortured Zhen severely to make him confess embezzling provisions for bribery; Zhen nearly died but never confessed.
translations.idiomatic: He also tortured Zhen to make him confess embezzling provisions for bribery; Zhen nearly died but never confessed.

sentences.zh: 淳用是免，珍竟論死，世威、震謫戍。

translations.literal: Chun was thereby spared; Zhen was sentenced to death, and Shiwei and Zhen were banished to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was spared; Zhen was sentenced to death, and Shiwei and Zhen were banished.

sentences.zh: 其後，俺答歲入寇，帝卒不悟，輒曰：「此銑欲開邊，故行報復耳。」

translations.literal: Afterwards Altan raided every year; the emperor never understood, but always said, "This is Xian wishing to open the frontier, so he takes revenge."
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards Altan raided every year; the emperor never understood, but always said, "This is Xian taking revenge for wishing to open the frontier."

sentences.zh: 丁汝夔，字大章，霑化人。

translations.literal: Ding Rukui, style name Dazhang, was a native of Zhanhua.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Rukui, whose style was Dazhang, came from Zhanhua.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhengde he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixteenth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，授禮部主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 爭「大禮」被杖，調吏部。

translations.literal: In disputing the "Grand Rites" he was beaten with the rod and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In disputing the Grand Rites controversy he was beaten with the rod and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 累官山西左布政使，擢右副都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: He rose to Left Administration Commissioner of Shanxi, was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and appointed grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Administration Commissioner of Shanxi, then Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 歷撫保定、應天。

translations.literal: He served successively as grand coordinator of Baoding and Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Grand Coordinator of Baoding and Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 入為左副都御史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 坐事調湖廣參政。

translations.literal: For an offense he was transferred to administration commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was transferred to administration commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 復以故官撫河南。

translations.literal: He was again appointed grand coordinator of Henan at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Grand Coordinator of Henan at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十八年十月拜兵部尚書兼督團營。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Minister of War with concurrent supervision of the regiment camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Minister of War with concurrent supervision of the regiment camps.

sentences.zh: 條上邊務十事，皆報可。

translations.literal: He submitted ten items on frontier affairs in detail; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten proposals on frontier affairs; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 當是時，俺答歲寇邊，羽書疊至。

translations.literal: At that time Altan raided the frontier every year and urgent dispatches arrived in piles.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Altan raided the frontier every year and urgent dispatches piled up.

sentences.zh: 天子方齋居西內，厭兵事，而大學士嚴嵩竊權，邊帥率以賄進，疆事大壞。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was then living in seclusion in the western palace, weary of military affairs, while Grand Secretary Yan Song usurped power; frontier commanders for the most part advanced through bribery, and frontier affairs were greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lived in seclusion in the western palace, weary of war, while Grand Secretary Yan Song usurped power; frontier commanders advanced through bribery, and frontier affairs collapsed.

sentences.zh: 其明年八月甲子，俺答犯宣府，諸將拒之不得入。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year, on the day jiazi, Altan violated Xuanfu; the generals resisted and he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the following year, on the day jiazi, Altan attacked Xuanfu; the generals held him off.

sentences.zh: 汝夔即上言：「寇不得誌於宣府，必東趨遼、薊。

translations.literal: Rukui immediately memorialized: "The bandits could not achieve their aim at Xuanfu and will surely turn east toward Liao and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui immediately memorialized: "Having failed at Xuanfu, the raiders will surely turn east toward Liao and Ji.

sentences.zh: 請敕諸將嚴為備。

translations.literal: I request that the generals be ordered to prepare strictly.
translations.idiomatic: I request that generals be ordered to prepare strictly.

sentences.zh: 潮河川乃陵京門戶，宜調遼東一軍赴白馬關，保定一軍赴古北口。」

translations.literal: Chaohe River is the gateway to the capital; a detachment from Liaodong should be sent to Baima Pass and one from Baoding to Gubeikou."
translations.idiomatic: Chaohe River is the gateway to the capital; a Liaodong detachment should go to Baima Pass and a Baoding detachment to Gubeikou."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 寇果引而東，駐大興州，去古北口百七十里。

translations.literal: The bandits did indeed turn east and encamped at Daxing Prefecture, one hundred seventy li from Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders did turn east and encamped at Daxing Prefecture, one hundred seventy li from Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 大同總兵官仇鸞知之，率所部馳至居庸南。

translations.literal: Qiu Luan, regional commander of Datong, learned of this and led his troops at speed to south of Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Luan, Regional Commander of Datong, learned of this and led his troops at speed south of Juyong.

sentences.zh: 順天巡撫王汝孝駐薊州，誤聽諜者謂寇向西北。

translations.literal: Wang Ruxiao, grand coordinator of Shuntian, was stationed at Jizhou and mistakenly believed spies who said the bandits were heading northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruxiao, Grand Coordinator of Shuntian, was at Jizhou and mistakenly believed spies who said the raiders were heading northwest.

sentences.zh: 汝夔信之，請令鸞還大同勿東，詔俟後報。

translations.literal: Rukui believed this and requested that Luan return to Datong and not go east; an edict ordered him to wait for later reports.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui believed this and asked that Luan return to Datong; an edict ordered him to wait for later reports.

sentences.zh: 及興州報至，命鸞壁居庸，汝孝守薊州。

translations.literal: When the report from Xingzhou arrived, Luan was ordered to hold Juyong and Ruxiao to defend Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the report from Xingzhou arrived, Luan was ordered to hold Juyong and Ruxiao to defend Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇循潮河川南下至古北口，薄關城。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits followed Chaohe River south to Gubeikou and pressed the pass city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the raiders followed Chaohe River south to Gubeikou and pressed the pass.

sentences.zh: 總兵官羅希韓、盧鉞不能卻，汝孝師大潰。

translations.literal: The regional commanders Luo Xihan and Lu Yue could not repel them; Ruxiao's army collapsed in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commanders Luo Xihan and Lu Yue could not repel them; Ruxiao's army collapsed in great defeat.

sentences.zh: 寇遂由石匣營達密雲，轉掠懷柔，圍順義城。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon passed through Shixia Camp to Miyun, turned to raid Huairou, and besieged Shunyi city.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders passed through Shixia Camp to Miyun, raided Huairou, and besieged Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 聞保定兵駐城內，乃解而南，至通州。

translations.literal: Hearing that Baoding troops were inside the city, they withdrew south to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Baoding troops were in the city, they withdrew south to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 阻白河不得渡，駐河東孤山，分剽昌平、三河，犯諸帝陵，殺掠不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Blocked by the Bai River and unable to cross, they encamped on Gushan east of the river, sent raiding parties to Changping and Sanhe, violated the imperial tombs, and killed and plundered beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked by the Bai River, they encamped on Gushan east of the river, raided Changping and Sanhe, violated imperial tombs, and killed and plundered beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 京師戒嚴，召各鎮勤王。

translations.literal: The capital was placed under martial alert and troops from all garrisons were summoned to aid the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was placed under martial alert and troops from all garrisons were summoned.

sentences.zh: 分遣文武大臣各九人，守京城九門，定西侯蔣傳、吏部侍郎王邦瑞總督之，而以錦衣都督陸炳，禮部侍郎王用賓，給事御史各四人，巡視皇城四門。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials great and small, nine of each, were dispatched to guard the nine gates of the capital; Marquis Jiang Chuan of Dingxi and Vice Minister Wang Bangrui supervised them, while Commander Lu Bing of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, Vice Minister Wang Yongbin, and four supervising secretaries and censors each inspected the four gates of the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: Nine civil and military officials each were dispatched to guard the capital's nine gates; Marquis Jiang Chuan of Dingxi and Vice Minister Wang Bangrui supervised, while Commander Lu Bing, Vice Minister Wang Yongbin, and four supervising secretaries and censors inspected the imperial city gates.

sentences.zh: 詔大小文臣知兵者，許汝夔委用。

translations.literal: An edict permitted Rukui to appoint civil officials great and small who understood military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted Rukui to appoint officials who understood military affairs.

sentences.zh: 汝夔條上八事，請列正兵四營於城外四隅，奇兵九營於九門外近郊。

translations.literal: Rukui submitted eight items, requesting four regular camps at the four corners outside the city and nine special camps in the suburbs outside the nine gates.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui submitted eight proposals, requesting four regular camps outside the city corners and nine special camps outside the nine gates.

sentences.zh: 正兵營各一萬，奇兵營各六千。

translations.literal: Each regular camp was to have ten thousand men, each special camp six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Each regular camp was to have ten thousand men, each special camp six thousand.

sentences.zh: 急遣大臣二人經略通州、涿州，且釋罪廢諸將使立功贖罪。

translations.literal: He urgently requested two senior officials to manage Tongzhou and Zhuozhou, and that dismissed and disgraced generals be released to achieve merit and redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently requested two senior officials for Tongzhou and Zhuozhou and that dismissed generals be released to redeem guilt through merit.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all.

sentences.zh: 然是時冊籍皆虛數。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the registers were all fictitious numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the registers were all fictitious numbers.

sentences.zh: 禁軍僅四五萬，老弱半之，又半役內外提督大臣家不歸伍，在伍者亦涕泣不敢前。

translations.literal: The forbidden army numbered only forty or fifty thousand; half were old and weak, and half were serving in the households of supervising grand eunuchs inside and outside and did not return to the ranks; those in the ranks also wept and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The forbidden army numbered only forty or fifty thousand; half were old and weak, and half served eunuch supervisors' households and never returned to ranks; those in ranks wept and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 從武庫索甲仗，主庫奄人勒常例，不時發。

translations.literal: When armor and weapons were requested from the armory, the eunuch in charge of the storehouse extorted customary fees and did not issue them in time.
translations.idiomatic: When armor was requested from the armory, the eunuch in charge extorted fees and did not issue it in time.

sentences.zh: 久之不能軍。

translations.literal: After a long time they still could not take the field.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time they still could not take the field.

sentences.zh: 乃發居民及四方應武舉諸生乘城，且大頒賞格。

translations.literal: Residents and candidates for military examinations from all quarters were then put on the walls, and great rewards were widely proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Residents and military examination candidates from all quarters were put on the walls and great rewards proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 仇鸞與副將徐玨、遊擊張騰等軍白河西，楊守謙與副將朱楫等軍東直門外，諸路援兵亦稍集。

translations.literal: Qiu Luan with Vice Commander Xu Yu and Raiding Commander Zhang Teng encamped west of the Bai River; Yang Shouqian with Vice Commander Zhu Ji encamped outside Dongzhimen; relief troops from various routes also gradually gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Luan with Vice Commander Xu Yu and Raiding Commander Zhang Teng camped west of the Bai River; Yang Shouqian with Vice Commander Zhu Ji outside Dongzhimen; relief troops gradually gathered.

sentences.zh: 議者率謂城內虛，城外有邊兵足恃，宜移京軍備內釁，汝夔亦以為然。

translations.literal: Debators for the most part said the interior was empty but frontier troops outside were sufficient; capital troops should be moved to guard against internal trouble, and Rukui also thought so.
translations.idiomatic: Most argued the interior was empty but frontier troops outside sufficed; capital troops should guard against internal trouble, and Rukui agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂量掣禁軍入營十王府、厭壽寺前。

translations.literal: Capital troops were then partially withdrawn into camps before the ten princely mansions and Yanshou Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Capital troops were partially withdrawn into camps before the ten princely mansions and Yanshou Temple.

sentences.zh: 掌營務者成國公朱希忠恐以兵少獲譴，乃東西抽掣為掩飾計。

translations.literal: Zhu Xizhong, Duke of Cheng who managed camp affairs, feared punishment for too few troops and shifted men east and west as a cover.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xizhong, Duke of Cheng who managed camps, feared blame for too few troops and shifted men east and west as cover.

sentences.zh: 士疲不得息，出怨言，而莫曉孰為調者，則爭詈汝夔。

translations.literal: Soldiers, exhausted without rest, uttered complaints, not knowing who had transferred them, and cursed Rukui.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers, exhausted without rest, complained without knowing who had transferred them, and cursed Rukui.

sentences.zh: 鸞兵無紀律，掠民間。

translations.literal: Luan's troops were without discipline and plundered the populace.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's troops lacked discipline and plundered civilians.

sentences.zh: 帝方眷鸞，令勿捕。

translations.literal: The emperor was then favoring Luan and ordered that they not be arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Luan and ordered they not be arrested.

sentences.zh: 汝夔亦戒勿治鸞兵。

translations.literal: Rukui also warned against punishing Luan's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui also warned against punishing Luan's troops.

sentences.zh: 民益怨怒。

translations.literal: The people grew all the more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: The people grew more resentful.

sentences.zh: 寇遊騎四出，去都城三十里。

translations.literal: The bandits' roaming cavalry went out in all directions thirty li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Raider cavalry ranged thirty li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 及辛巳，遂自通州渡河而西，前鋒七百騎駐安定門外教場。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi they crossed from Tongzhou to the west; seven hundred horsemen of the vanguard encamped at the drill ground outside Anding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi they crossed from Tongzhou westward; seven hundred vanguard horsemen encamped at the drill ground outside Anding Gate.

sentences.zh: 明日，大營薄都城。

translations.literal: The next day the main camp pressed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the main camp pressed the capital.

sentences.zh: 分掠西山、黃村、沙河、大小榆河，畿甸大震。

translations.literal: They raided separately in Xishan, Huangcun, Shahe, and the great and small Yu Rivers; the metropolitan region was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Xishan, Huangcun, Shahe, and the Yu Rivers; the metropolitan region was shaken.

sentences.zh: 初，寇逼通州，部所遣偵卒出城不數里，道遇傷者，輒奔還妄言誑汝夔。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the bandits pressed Tongzhou, scouts dispatched by the ministry went only a few li beyond the city; whenever they met the wounded they fled back and falsely deceived Rukui.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders pressed Tongzhou, ministry scouts went only a few li out; meeting the wounded they fled back and deceived Rukui.

sentences.zh: 既而言不讎，汝夔弗罪也。

translations.literal: When their words were not verified, Rukui did not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: When their reports proved false, Rukui did not punish them.

sentences.zh: 募他卒偵之復如前。

translations.literal: Other scouts were recruited and behaved the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: Other scouts behaved the same.

sentences.zh: 以故寇眾寡遠近皆不能知。

translations.literal: Therefore whether the enemy were many or few, near or far, could not be known.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the enemy's strength and distance could not be known.

sentences.zh: 宣府總兵官趙國忠，參將趙臣、孫時謙、袁正，遊擊姚冕，山西遊擊羅恭等，各以兵入援，營玉河諸處。

translations.literal: Zhao Guozhong, regional commander of Xuanfu, Battalion Commanders Zhao Chen, Sun Shiqian, and Yuan Zheng, Raiding Commander Yao Mian, Shanxi Raiding Commander Luo Gong, and others each led troops to aid and encamped at Yuhe and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guozhong of Xuanfu, Zhao Chen, Sun Shiqian, Yuan Zheng, Yao Mian, Luo Gong of Shanxi, and others led relief troops and encamped at Yuhe.

sentences.zh: 詔兵部核諸鎮兵數，行賞賚。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of War to verify troop numbers from all garrisons and issue rewards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of War to verify garrison troop numbers and issue rewards.

sentences.zh: 勤王兵先後五六萬人，皆聞變即赴，未賫糗糧。

translations.literal: Relief troops, fifty or sixty thousand in all arriving before and after, all hurried at news of the alarm without carrying rations.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops, fifty or sixty thousand in all, hurried at the alarm without rations.

sentences.zh: 制下犒師，牛酒無所出。

translations.literal: When orders came down to reward the army, there was no beef or wine to give.
translations.idiomatic: When orders came to reward the army, there was no beef or wine.

sentences.zh: 越二三日，援軍始得數餅餌，益饑疲不任戰。

translations.literal: After two or three days the relief army received only a few cakes and grew hungrier, more exhausted, and unfit for battle.
translations.idiomatic: After two or three days they received only a few cakes and grew hungrier, exhausted, and unfit for battle.

sentences.zh: 帝久不視朝，軍事無由面白。

translations.literal: The emperor had long not held court and military affairs could not be reported face to face.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long not held court and military affairs could not be reported in person.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多以為言，帝不許。

translations.literal: Court officials repeatedly spoke of this; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials repeatedly spoke of this; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書徐階復固請，帝乃許。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Jie again firmly requested; the emperor then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Xu Jie firmly requested again; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 癸未，群臣昧爽入。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei all officials entered before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei officials entered before dawn.

sentences.zh: 至日晡，帝始禦奉天殿，不發一詞，但命階奉敕諭至午門，集群臣切責之而已。

translations.literal: Not until mid-afternoon did the emperor appear at Fengtian Hall, uttering not a word but only ordering Jie to deliver an edict at Meridian Gate scolding the officials severely.
translations.idiomatic: Not until mid-afternoon did the emperor appear at Fengtian Hall, uttering not a word but ordering Jie to deliver an edict at Meridian Gate scolding officials severely.

sentences.zh: 帝怒文武臣不任事，尤怒汝夔。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that civil and military officials were incompetent and especially angry with Rukui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry that officials were incompetent and especially angry with Rukui.

sentences.zh: 吏部因請起楊守禮、劉源清、史道、許論於家。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel thereupon requested that Yang Shouli, Liu Yuanqing, Shi Dao, and Xu Lun be recalled from retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel requested recall of Yang Shouli, Liu Yuanqing, Shi Dao, and Xu Lun from retirement.

sentences.zh: 汝夔不自安，請督諸將出城戰，而以侍郎謝蘭署部事。

translations.literal: Rukui, ill at ease, requested to supervise the generals in going out to fight, with Vice Minister Xie Lan acting as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Rukui asked to lead generals out to fight, with Vice Minister Xie Lan acting as minister.

sentences.zh: 帝責其推委，命居中如故。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed him for shirking and ordered him to remain at his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed him for shirking and ordered him to remain as before.

sentences.zh: 寇縱橫內地八日，諸軍不敢發一矢。

translations.literal: The bandits ranged across the interior eight days; the armies did not dare loose a single arrow.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders ranged the interior eight days; armies did not loose a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 寇本無意攻城，且所掠過望，乃整輜重，從容趨白羊口而去。

translations.literal: The bandits had never intended to attack the city, and having plundered beyond expectation, they gathered their baggage and leisurely headed for Baiyangkou to depart.
translations.idiomatic: They never intended to attack the city; having plundered beyond expectation, they gathered baggage and leisurely departed through Baiyangkou.

sentences.zh: 方事棘，帝趣諸將戰甚急。

translations.literal: When affairs were critical the emperor urgently pressed the generals to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were critical the emperor urgently pressed generals to fight.

sentences.zh: 汝夔以咨嵩。

translations.literal: Rukui consulted Song.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui consulted Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「塞上敗或可掩也，失利輦下，帝無不知，誰執其咎？

translations.literal: Song said: "Defeat on the frontier may be concealed, but defeat below the imperial carriage—the emperor will surely know. Who will bear the blame?
translations.idiomatic: Song said: "Defeat on the frontier may be concealed, but defeat below the imperial carriage—the emperor will know. Who bears the blame?

sentences.zh: 寇飽自飏去耳。」

translations.literal: The bandits are sated and will depart of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The raiders are sated and will depart of themselves."

sentences.zh: 汝夔因不敢主戰，諸將亦益閉營，寇以此肆掠無所忌。

translations.literal: Rukui therefore dared not advocate battle; the generals also increasingly closed their camps, and the bandits plundered without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui dared not advocate battle; generals closed their camps, and raiders plundered without restraint.

sentences.zh: 既退，汝夔、蘭及戶、工尚書李士翺、胡松，侍郎駱颙、孫禬皆引罪。

translations.literal: After they withdrew, Rukui, Lan, and Ministers of Revenue and Works Li Shi'ang and Hu Song, and Vice Ministers Luo Yang and Sun Qi all cited their offenses.
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawal, Rukui, Lan, Ministers Li Shi'ang and Hu Song, and Vice Ministers Luo Yang and Sun Qi all cited offenses.

sentences.zh: 命革士翺職，停松俸，俱戴罪辦事，侍郎各停俸五月，而下汝夔獄。

translations.literal: Li Shi'ang was removed from office, Hu Song's salary suspended, all to continue duties bearing guilt; vice ministers' salary suspended five months; Rukui was sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'ang was removed, Song's salary suspended, all continuing under guilt; vice ministers suspended five months; Rukui was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 帝欲大行誅以懲後。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to execute widely to warn posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to execute widely as a warning.

sentences.zh: 汝夔窘，求救於嵩。

translations.literal: Rukui, cornered, begged Song for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Rukui begged Song for rescue.

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「我在，必不令公死。」

translations.literal: Song said: "While I am here, I will certainly not let you die."
translations.idiomatic: Song said: "While I am here, you will certainly not die."

sentences.zh: 及見帝怒甚，竟不敢言。

translations.literal: Yet when he saw the emperor's great anger, he ultimately dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yet seeing the emperor's great anger, he dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 給事御史劾汝夔禦寇無策。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors impeached Rukui for having no strategy against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached Rukui for having no strategy against the raiders.

sentences.zh: 帝責其不早言，奪俸有差。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed him for not speaking earlier and reduced salary by varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed him for not speaking earlier and reduced salary.

sentences.zh: 趣具獄，怒法司奏當緩，杖都御史屠僑、刑部侍郎彭黯、大理卿沈良才各四十，降俸五等。

translations.literal: He urged completion of the case; angry that the judicial offices recommended leniency, he had Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao, Vice Minister Peng An, and Chief Director Shen Liangcai each beaten forty times and salary reduced five grades.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the case completed; angry at recommended leniency, he had Tu Qiao, Peng An, and Shen Liangcai beaten forty times and salary reduced five grades.

sentences.zh: 刑科張侃等循故事覆奏，各杖五十，斥侃為民。

translations.literal: Zhang Kan and others of the penal section memorialized in review according to precedent; each was beaten fifty times and Kan reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kan and others memorialized in review; each was beaten fifty times and Kan dismissed.

sentences.zh: 坐汝夔守備不設，即日斬於市，梟其首，妻流三千里，子戍鐵嶺。

translations.literal: Rukui was sentenced for failing to prepare defenses and beheaded in the market that day; his head was displayed, his wife exiled three thousand li, his son banished to Tieling.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui was sentenced for failing to prepare defenses, beheaded that day, his head displayed, wife exiled three thousand li, son banished to Tieling.

sentences.zh: 汝夔臨刑，始悔為嵩所賣。

translations.literal: At execution Rukui finally regretted being sold out by Song.
translations.idiomatic: At execution Rukui regretted being sold out by Song.

sentences.zh: 方廷訊時，職方郎王尚學當從坐。

translations.literal: During court trial, Bureau Director Wang Shangxue was to be implicated.
translations.idiomatic: During trial, Bureau Director Wang Shangxue was to be implicated.

sentences.zh: 汝夔曰，「罪在尚書，郎中無預」，得減死論戍。

translations.literal: Rukui said, "The guilt lies with the minister; the bureau director has no part," and Shangxue received reduced sentence to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui said, "Guilt lies with the minister, not the director," and Shangxue received banishment instead of death.

sentences.zh: 比赴市，問左右：「王郎中免乎？」

translations.literal: On the way to execution he asked those beside him: "Is Bureau Director Wang spared?"
translations.idiomatic: Going to execution he asked: "Is Bureau Director Wang spared?"

sentences.zh: 尚學子化適在旁，謝曰：「荷公恩，免矣。」

translations.literal: Shangxue's son Hua happened to be nearby and thanked him: "Thanks to your grace, he is spared."
translations.idiomatic: Shangxue's son Hua thanked him: "Thanks to your grace, he is spared."

sentences.zh: 汝夔嘆曰：「汝父勸我速戰，我為政府誤。

translations.literal: Rukui sighed: "Your father urged me to fight quickly; I was misled by the government.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui sighed: "Your father urged quick battle; I was misled by the government.

sentences.zh: 汝父免，我死無恨。」

translations.literal: Your father is spared; I die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Your father is spared; I die without regret."

sentences.zh: 聞者為泣下。

translations.literal: Hearers wept.
translations.idiomatic: Hearers wept.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing his office was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 汝夔既下獄，並逮汝孝、希韓、鉞。

translations.literal: After Rukui was imprisoned, Ruxiao, Xihan, and Yue were also arrested.
translations.idiomatic: After Rukui was imprisoned, Ruxiao, Xihan, and Yue were also arrested.

sentences.zh: 寇未盡去，官校不敢前，托言汝孝等追寇白羊口，遠不可卒至。

translations.literal: The bandits had not fully departed and the court officers dared not advance, making the excuse that Ruxiao and the others were pursuing the bandits at Baiyangkou and could not arrive quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders had not fully departed and court officers dared not advance, claiming Ruxiao and others were pursuing them at Baiyangkou.

sentences.zh: 比逮至，論死。

translations.literal: When they were arrested, they were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When arrested, they were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 帝怒漸解，而汝孝復以首功聞，命俱減死戍邊。

translations.literal: As the emperor's anger gradually eased, Ruxiao was again reported for chief merit; all were ordered to have death reduced to banishment on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's anger eased, Ruxiao was reported for chief merit; all received reduced sentences to frontier banishment.

sentences.zh: 楊守謙，字允亨，徐州人。

translations.literal: Yang Shouqian, style name Yunheng, was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouqian, whose style was Yunheng, came from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父誌學，字遜夫，弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: His father Zhixue, style name Xunfu, became a jinshi in the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhixue, whose style was Xunfu, passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 巡撫大同、寧夏，邊人愛之。

translations.literal: He served as grand coordinator of Datong and Ningxia; the frontier people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Coordinator of Datong and Ningxia; frontier people loved him.

sentences.zh: 累官刑部尚書，卒，謚康惠。

translations.literal: He rose to Minister of Punishments and died; he was given the posthumous name Kanghui.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Punishments and died; his posthumous name was Kanghui.

sentences.zh: 守謙登嘉靖八年進士，授屯田主事。

translations.literal: Shouqian passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of Jiajing and was appointed principal clerk for land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of Jiajing and was appointed principal clerk for land tax.

sentences.zh: 改職方，歷郎中，練習兵計。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military affairs, served as bureau director, and studied military planning.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to military affairs, served as bureau director, and studied military planning.

sentences.zh: 出為陜西副使，改督學政，有聲，就拜參政。

translations.literal: He went out as vice commissioner of Shaanxi, was transferred to education commissioner, gained renown, and was appointed administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice commissioner of Shaanxi, then education commissioner, gained renown, and was appointed administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未任，擢右僉都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: Before taking office he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 上言偏頭、老營堡二所，余地千九百余頃，請興舉營田。

translations.literal: He memorialized that at the two posts of Piantou and Laoying Fort there were more than nineteen hundred qing of surplus land and requested development of military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Piantou and Laoying Fort had more than nineteen hundred qing of surplus land and requested military colonies.

sentences.zh: 因薦副使張鎬為提調，牛種取給本土。

translations.literal: He recommended Vice Commissioner Zhang Hao as supervisor, with oxen and seed taken locally.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Vice Commissioner Zhang Hao as supervisor, with oxen and seed from local sources.

sentences.zh: 帝稱為忠，即報可。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this as loyal and immediately approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this as loyal and approved immediately.

sentences.zh: 俄移撫延綏。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand coordinator of Yan-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Grand Coordinator of Yan-Sui.

sentences.zh: 請久任鎬，終其事。

translations.literal: He requested that Hao serve long to complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that Hao serve long enough to complete the work.

sentences.zh: 其後二年，營田大興。

translations.literal: Two years later military colonies flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later military colonies flourished.

sentences.zh: 計秋獲可當帑銀十萬，邊關谷價減十五。

translations.literal: It was calculated that the autumn harvest could equal one hundred thousand taels of treasury silver and frontier grain prices fell fifteen percent.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn harvest was calculated to equal one hundred thousand taels of treasury silver and frontier grain prices fell fifteen percent.

sentences.zh: 守謙薦鎬可大用，且言延綏、安定諸邊可如例。

translations.literal: Shouqian recommended Hao for greater appointment and said Yan-Sui, Anding, and other frontiers could follow the same model.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian recommended Hao for greater appointment and said Yan-Sui, Anding, and other frontiers could follow the model.

sentences.zh: 戶部請推行之九邊。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue requested extension to the nine frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue requested extension to the nine frontiers.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，命亟行之，錄守謙、鎬功。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, ordered rapid implementation, and recorded the achievements of Shouqian and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, ordered rapid implementation, and recorded Shouqian and Hao's achievements.

sentences.zh: 守謙未去延綏，而鎬已巡撫寧夏矣。

translations.literal: Shouqian had not yet left Yan-Sui when Hao was already grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian had not yet left Yan-Sui when Hao was already Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 守謙至延綏，言：「激勸軍士在重賞。

translations.literal: When Shouqian reached Yan-Sui he said: "Encouraging soldiers lies in heavy rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouqian reached Yan-Sui he said: "Encouraging soldiers lies in heavy rewards.

sentences.zh: 令斬一首者升一級，不願者予白金三十兩。

translations.literal: The order was that beheading one head merited promotion one grade, or for those unwilling, thirty taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Beheading one head merited one grade of promotion, or thirty taels of silver for those unwilling.

sentences.zh: 賞已薄，又文移察勘，動涉歲時，以故士心不勸。

translations.literal: Rewards were already meager, and documentary verification dragged on for years, so soldiers' hearts were not encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were meager and verification dragged on for years, so soldiers were not encouraged.

sentences.zh: 近宣、大事棘稍加賞格，請倍增其數，鎮巡官驗明即給。

translations.literal: Recently Xuan and Da affairs were critical and rewards were slightly increased; I request doubling the amounts, with frontier officials verifying and paying at once.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Xuan and Da were critical and rewards increased slightly; I request doubling amounts with immediate payment after verification.

sentences.zh: 蓋增級、襲蔭，有官者利之，窮卒覬賞而已。」

translations.literal: For promotion in grade and hereditary privilege, those with office benefit; poor soldiers only hope for reward."
translations.idiomatic: Promotion and hereditary privilege benefit officers; poor soldiers only hope for cash reward."

sentences.zh: 兵部以為然，定斬首一級者與五十兩，著為令。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War agreed and fixed fifty taels for one severed head as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War agreed and fixed fifty taels per head as regulation.

sentences.zh: 以前山西修邊功，增俸一級，賜金幣有加。

translations.literal: For earlier achievements in repairing the Shanxi frontier, his salary was increased one grade and gold and silks bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: For repairing the Shanxi frontier, his salary increased one grade and he received gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 請給新設遊兵月餉，發倉儲貸饑卒，皆報許。

translations.literal: He requested monthly pay for newly established mobile troops and grain loans for starving soldiers; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He requested monthly pay for new mobile troops and grain loans for starving soldiers; all approved.

sentences.zh: 二十九年進副都御史，巡撫保定兼督紫荊諸關。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Baoding with supervision of the Zijing passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of Baoding with supervision of Zijing passes.

sentences.zh: 去鎮之日，傾城號泣，有追送數百里外者。

translations.literal: On the day he left his post the whole city wept aloud; some pursued him several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When he left his post the whole city wept; some followed him hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 未幾，俺答入寇，守謙率師倍道入援。

translations.literal: Before long Altan invaded; Shouqian led his army at double speed to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Altan invaded; Shouqian led his army at double speed to aid the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其至，甚喜，令營崇文門外。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing he had arrived, was greatly pleased and ordered him to encamp outside Chongwen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing he had arrived, the emperor was pleased and ordered him to encamp outside Chongwen Gate.

sentences.zh: 會副總兵朱楫，參將祝福、馮登亦各以兵至，人心稍安。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Zhu Ji and Battalion Commanders Zhu Fu and Feng Deng also arrived with troops; popular sentiment grew somewhat calmer.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Zhu Ji and Battalion Commanders Zhu Fu and Feng Deng arrived; popular sentiment calmed somewhat.

sentences.zh: 寇遊騎散掠枯柳諸村，去京城二十里。

translations.literal: Raider cavalry scattered to plunder Koliu and other villages twenty li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Raider cavalry plundered Koliu and other villages twenty li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 守謙及楫等兵移營東直門外。

translations.literal: Shouqian and Ji moved their camps outside Dongzhimen.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian and Ji moved camps outside Dongzhimen.

sentences.zh: 詔同仇鸞調度京城及各路援兵，相機戰守。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them together with Qiu Luan to coordinate capital and relief troops and fight or defend as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them with Qiu Luan to coordinate capital and relief troops.

sentences.zh: 寇薄都城，諸將高秉元、徐鏞等禦之，不能卻。

translations.literal: When the bandits pressed the capital, Generals Gao Bingyuan, Xu Yong, and others resisted but could not repel them.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders pressed the capital, Generals Gao Bingyuan and Xu Yong could not repel them.

sentences.zh: 帝拜鸞大將軍，進守謙兵部右侍郎，協同提督內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Luan grand general and promoted Shouqian to Vice Minister of War to jointly supervise internal and external military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Luan grand general and promoted Shouqian to Vice Minister of War to jointly supervise military affairs.

sentences.zh: 鸞時自孤山還，至東直門觀望，斬死人首六級，報功。

translations.literal: Luan had returned from Gushan to Dongzhimen to observe, beheaded six dead men's heads, and reported merit.
translations.idiomatic: Luan returned from Gushan to Dongzhimen, beheaded six corpses, and reported merit.

sentences.zh: 守謙孤軍薄俺答營，而陣無後繼，不敢戰。

translations.literal: Shouqian led a lone army close to Altan's camp but his formation had no reserve and he dared not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian led a lone army near Altan's camp but had no reserve and dared not fight.

sentences.zh: 帝聞不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this with displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard with displeasure.

sentences.zh: 而尚書丁汝夔慮喪師，戒勿輕戰。

translations.literal: Minister Ding Rukui, fearing loss of the army, warned against light battle.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ding Rukui, fearing defeat, warned against light battle.

sentences.zh: 諸將離城遠，見守謙不戰，亦堅壁，輒引汝夔及守謙為辭。

translations.literal: Generals far from the city, seeing Shouqian not fight, also held their walls and cited Rukui and Shouqian as excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Generals far from the city, seeing Shouqian not fight, held their walls and cited Rukui and Shouqian.

sentences.zh: 流聞禁中，帝益怒。

translations.literal: Rumors reached the palace and the emperor grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors reached the palace and the emperor grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 初，寇抵安定門，詔守謙與楫等合擊，莫敢前。

translations.literal: Earlier when the bandits reached Anding Gate, an edict ordered Shouqian and Ji to attack together; none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders reached Anding Gate, an edict ordered Shouqian and Ji to attack; none advanced.

sentences.zh: 守謙亦委無部檄，第申儆備。

translations.literal: Shouqian also pleaded lack of ministry dispatch and only reported heightened preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian pleaded lack of ministry dispatch and only reported heightened preparedness.

sentences.zh: 寇遂毀城外廬舍。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon destroyed outer buildings.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders destroyed outer buildings.

sentences.zh: 城西北隅火光燭天，內臣園宅在焉，環泣帝前，稱將帥為文臣制，故寇得至此。

translations.literal: Firelight in the northwest corner of the city lit the sky; eunuchs' gardens were there and they wept before the emperor, saying generals were restrained by civil officials, hence the bandits reached here.
translations.idiomatic: Fire lit the northwest corner where eunuchs' gardens lay; they wept before the emperor, blaming civil officials for restraining generals.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「守謙擁眾自全，朕親降旨趣戰，何得以部檄為解。」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Shouqian holds the crowd to preserve himself; I personally issued edicts urging battle—how can he use lack of ministry dispatch as excuse?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily: "Shouqian preserves himself; I personally ordered battle—how can he cite lack of ministry dispatch?

sentences.zh: 寇退，遂執守謙與汝夔廷鞫之。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, Shouqian and Rukui were arrested and tried at court.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders withdrew, Shouqian and Rukui were tried at court.

sentences.zh: 坐失誤軍機，即日戮於市。

translations.literal: Convicted of mishandling military affairs, they were executed in the market that day.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of mishandling military affairs, they were executed that day.

sentences.zh: 守謙臨刑時，慨然曰：「臣以勤王反獲罪，讒賊之口實蔽聖聰。

translations.literal: At execution Shouqian said with feeling: "I came to aid the throne yet am punished; slanderers' mouths truly blind the sage ear.
translations.idiomatic: At execution Shouqian said: "I came to aid the throne yet am punished; slander blinds the sage ear.

sentences.zh: 皇天後土知臣此心，死何恨。」

translations.literal: Heaven and earth know my heart; I die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth know my heart; I die without regret.

sentences.zh: 邊陲吏士知守謙死，無不流涕者。

translations.literal: Frontier officials and soldiers, learning of Shouqian's death, all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials and soldiers all wept at Shouqian's death.

sentences.zh: 守謙坦易無城府，馭下多恩意。

translations.literal: Shouqian was open and without hidden designs; in governing subordinates he showed much kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian was open and without hidden designs; he showed much kindness to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 守官廉，位至開府，蕭然若寒士。

translations.literal: In office he was incorrupt; though he reached grand coordinator rank, he lived plainly as a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Incorrupt in office, though grand coordinator, he lived plainly as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 然性遲重，客有勸之戰者，應曰：「周亞夫何人乎？」

translations.literal: Yet his nature was slow and heavy; when a guest urged battle he replied: "Who was Zhou Yafu?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was slow by nature; when urged to fight he asked: "Who was Zhou Yafu?

sentences.zh: 客曰：「公誤矣，今日何得比漢法？」

translations.literal: The guest said: "Sir is mistaken—how can today be compared to Han law?"
translations.idiomatic: The guest said: "You are mistaken—today cannot be compared to Han law."

sentences.zh: 守謙不納，竟得罪。

translations.literal: Shouqian would not accept this and ultimately suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian would not accept and ultimately suffered punishment.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈兵部尚書，謚恪湣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously made Minister of War with the posthumous name Kemin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously made Minister of War with posthumous name Kemin.

sentences.zh: 商大節，字孟堅，鐘祥人。

translations.literal: Shang Dajie, style name Mengjian, was a native of Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Dajie, whose style was Mengjian, came from Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授豐城知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 始為築城，捕境內盜幾盡。

translations.literal: He first built the city wall and captured nearly all bandits within the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He first built the city wall and captured nearly all local bandits.

sentences.zh: 擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the military section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the military section.

sentences.zh: 京察竣，復命科道互相劾，被謫鹽城縣丞。

translations.literal: After the capital evaluation, censorial officials were again ordered to impeach one another; he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital evaluation, censorial officials impeached one another; he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 三遷刑部郎中，出為廣東僉事。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became bureau director in the Ministry of Punishments and went out as vice commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became bureau director in the Ministry of Punishments and vice commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 搗海南叛黎巢，增秩，賜金幣。

translations.literal: He destroyed rebel Li nests in Hainan, received increased rank, and was rewarded with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed rebel Li nests in Hainan, received increased rank, and gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 累官山東按察使。

translations.literal: He rose to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 擢右僉都御史，巡撫保定兼提督紫刑諸關。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Baoding with supervision of the Zijing passes.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of Baoding with supervision of Zijing passes.

sentences.zh: 慮俺答內侵，疏請重根本，護神京。

translations.literal: Fearing Altan's invasion, he memorialized to strengthen the foundation and protect the divine capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Altan's invasion, he memorialized to strengthen foundations and protect the capital.

sentences.zh: 居四年，召理院事。

translations.literal: After four years he was summoned to manage court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was summoned to manage court affairs.

sentences.zh: 俺答果大舉薄都城。

translations.literal: Altan did indeed raid in force and press the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Altan did raid in force and press the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔城中居民及四方入應武舉者悉登陴守，以大節率五城御史統之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered capital residents and military examination candidates from all quarters to mount the walls; Dajie led the five-city censors to command them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered residents and examination candidates onto the walls; Dajie led five-city censors to command them.

sentences.zh: 發帑金五千兩，命便宜募壯士。

translations.literal: Five thousand taels from the treasury were issued for him to recruit warriors at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand taels were issued for recruiting warriors at discretion.

sentences.zh: 屢條上軍民急務。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted urgent matters for army and people.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted urgent matters for army and people.

sentences.zh: 比寇退，復命兼管民兵，經略京城內外。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew he was again ordered to manage militia and oversee inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders withdrew he was ordered to manage militia inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 訓練鼓舞，軍容甚壯。

translations.literal: Through training and encouragement, military appearance was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Through training and encouragement, military appearance was imposing.

sentences.zh: 擢右副都御史，經略如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief with oversight unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief with oversight unchanged.

sentences.zh: 所募民兵已四千，請以三等授餉。

translations.literal: Militia recruited already numbered four thousand; he requested three grades of pay.
translations.idiomatic: Militia recruited numbered four thousand; he requested three grades of pay.

sentences.zh: 上者月二石，其次遞減五鬥。

translations.literal: The highest received two shi monthly, the next decreasing by five dou.
translations.idiomatic: The highest received two shi monthly, the next decreasing by five dou.

sentences.zh: 帝亟從之。

translations.literal: The emperor quickly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quickly approved.

sentences.zh: 仇鸞為大將軍，盡統中外兵馬，惡大節獨為一軍，不受其節制，欲困之。

translations.literal: Qiu Luan as grand general controlled all internal and external troops and hated Dajie's independent army not under his command, wishing to trap him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Luan as grand general controlled all troops and hated Dajie's independent army, wishing to trap him.

sentences.zh: 乃請畫地分守，以京師四郊委大節。

translations.literal: He requested demarcated defense, assigning the four suburbs of the capital to Dajie.
translations.idiomatic: He requested demarcated defense, assigning the capital's four suburbs to Dajie.

sentences.zh: 大節言：「臣雖經略京城，實非有重兵專戰守責者也。

translations.literal: Dajie said: "Though I oversee the capital, I truly have no heavy troops with sole responsibility for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Dajie said: "Though I oversee the capital, I have no heavy troops with sole battle responsibility.

sentences.zh: 京城四郊利害，鸞欲專以臣當。

translations.literal: The advantages and harms of the four suburbs Luan wishes to assign entirely to me.
translations.idiomatic: Luan wishes to assign all risks of the four suburbs to me.

sentences.zh: 臣節制者，止巡捕軍，鸞又頻調遣，奸宄猝發，誰為捍禦哉？」

translations.literal: What I command is only patrol troops, yet Luan repeatedly requisitions them—when sudden trouble arises, who will defend?
translations.idiomatic: I command only patrol troops, yet Luan requisitions them—when trouble arises, who defends?

sentences.zh: 所爭甚晰，而帝方寵鸞，不欲人撓其事，責大節懷奸避難，立下詔獄。

translations.literal: His argument was very clear, but the emperor favored Luan and did not wish others to interfere; he blamed Dajie for treacherous evasion and sent him to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: His argument was clear, but the emperor favored Luan; he blamed Dajie for evasion and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 法司希旨，當大節斬。

translations.literal: The judicial offices curried favor and sentenced Dajie to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial offices curried favor and sentenced Dajie to execution.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩言：「大節誠有罪，但法司引律非是。

translations.literal: Yan Song said: "Dajie is indeed guilty, but the judicial offices' citation of statutes is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song said: "Dajie is guilty, but the statutes cited are incorrect.

sentences.zh: 幸赦其死，戍極邊。」

translations.literal: I beg mercy on his life and banishment to the remotest frontier."
translations.idiomatic: I beg mercy—banish him to the remotest frontier."

sentences.zh: 亦不聽。

translations.literal: This was also not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This was also rejected.

sentences.zh: 時三十年四月也。

translations.literal: This was in the fourth month of the thirtieth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fourth month of the thirtieth year.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，鸞死，大節故部曲石鏜、孫九思等數百人伏闕訟冤，章再上。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year Luan died; Dajie's former troops Shi Tong, Sun Jiusi, and several hundred others knelt at the palace gate pleading injustice, memorials submitted repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Luan died; Dajie's former troops knelt at the palace gate pleading injustice.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎張時徹等言：「大節為逆鸞制肘，以抵於法，乞順群情赦之。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhang Shiche and others said: "Dajie was constrained by the traitor Luan and thus fell under the law; I beg follow popular sentiment and pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhang Shiche said Dajie was constrained by Luan and begged pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，鐫時徹二秩。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and reduced Shiche two grades.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and reduced Shiche two grades.

sentences.zh: 明年竟卒於獄。

translations.literal: The next year Dajie still died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Dajie died in prison.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復故官，贈兵部尚書，謚端湣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was restored to his former office, posthumously made Minister of War, with the posthumous name Duanmin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored; he was posthumously made Minister of War with posthumous name Duanmin.

sentences.zh: 王忬，字民應，太倉人。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, style name Minying, was a native of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, whose style was Minying, came from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 父倬，南京兵部右侍郎，以謹厚稱。

translations.literal: His father Zhuo was Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing, known for prudence and honesty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuo was Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing, known for prudence and honesty.

sentences.zh: 忬登嘉靖二十年進士，授行人，遷御史。

translations.literal: Yu passed the metropolitan examination in the twentieth year of Jiajing, was appointed courier, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu passed the metropolitan examination in the twentieth year of Jiajing, served as courier, then censor.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出閣，疏以武宗居青宮為戒。

translations.literal: When the crown prince left the palace school, he memorialized taking Emperor Wuzong's residence in the Eastern Palace as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince left the palace school, he warned against repeating Emperor Wuzong's conduct in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 又劾罷東廠太監宋興。

translations.literal: He also impeached and removed the Eastern Depot eunuch Song Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached and removed Eastern Depot eunuch Song Xing.

sentences.zh: 出視河東鹽政，以疾歸。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect salt administration in Hedong and returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected salt administration in Hedong and returned home ill.

sentences.zh: 已，起按湖廣，復按順天。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed to inspect Huguang and again inspected Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inspected Huguang and again Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，俺答大舉犯古北口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Altan raided in force and violated Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Altan raided in force at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 忬奏言潮河川有徑道，一日夜可達通州。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized that Chaohe River had a shortcut by which one could reach Tongzhou in a day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized that Chaohe River had a shortcut reaching Tongzhou in a day and night.

sentences.zh: 因疾馳至通為守禦計，盡徙舟楫之在東岸者。

translations.literal: He hurried to Tongzhou despite illness to prepare defenses and moved all boats on the east bank.
translations.idiomatic: Despite illness he hurried to Tongzhou to prepare defenses and moved all boats on the east bank.

sentences.zh: 夜半，寇果大至。

translations.literal: At midnight the bandits indeed arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the raiders arrived in force.

sentences.zh: 不得渡，遂壁於河東。

translations.literal: Unable to cross, they encamped east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to cross, they encamped east of the river.

sentences.zh: 帝密遣中使覘軍，見忬方厲士乘城。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly sent a palace agent to observe the army and saw Yu sternly encouraging soldiers on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace agent to observe and saw Yu encouraging soldiers on the wall.

sentences.zh: 還奏，帝大喜。

translations.literal: On reporting back the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On reporting back the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 副都御史王儀守通州，御史姜廷頤劾其不職，忬亦言儀縱士卒虐大同軍。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yi guarded Tongzhou; Censor Jiang Tingyi impeached him for incompetence, and Yu also said Yi allowed soldiers to abuse Datong troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi guarded Tongzhou; Censor Jiang Tingyi impeached him, and Yu said Yi allowed soldiers to abuse Datong troops.

sentences.zh: 大同軍者，仇鸞兵也。

translations.literal: The Datong troops were Qiu Luan's soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They were Qiu Luan's soldiers.

sentences.zh: 帝立命逮儀，而超擢忬右僉都御史代之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered Yi arrested and abruptly promoted Yu to Right Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yi arrested and abruptly promoted Yu to Right Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 寇退，忬請振難民，築京師外郭，修通州城，築張家灣大小二堡，置沿河敵臺。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, Yu requested relief for refugees, building the outer wall of the capital, repairing Tongzhou city, building large and small forts at Zhangjiawan, and setting beacon towers along the river—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders withdrew, Yu requested refugee relief, outer capital walls, Tongzhou repairs, Zhangjiawan forts, and river beacons—all approved.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 尋罷通州、易州守禦大臣，召忬還。

translations.literal: Soon the defending ministers of Tongzhou and Yizhou were dismissed and Yu was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon defending ministers of Tongzhou and Yizhou were dismissed and Yu recalled.

sentences.zh: 三十一年出撫山東。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he went out as grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he became Grand Coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 甫三月，以浙江倭寇亟，命忬提督軍務，巡視浙江及福、興、漳、泉四府。

translations.literal: After only three months, because Japanese pirates in Zhejiang were urgent, Yu was ordered to supervise military affairs and inspect Zhejiang and the four prefectures of Fu, Xing, Zhang, and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: After three months, Japanese pirates in Zhejiang grew urgent; Yu was ordered to supervise military affairs in Zhejiang and four Fujian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 先後上方略十二事，任參將俞大猷、湯克寬，又奏釋參將尹鳳、盧鏜系。

translations.literal: He submitted twelve strategic proposals in succession, entrusted Battalion Commanders Yu Dayou and Tang Kekuan, and memorialized release of imprisoned Battalion Commanders Yin Feng and Lu Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted twelve strategies, entrusted Yu Dayou and Tang Kekuan, and memorialized release of Yin Feng and Lu Zhen.

sentences.zh: 賊犯溫州，克寬破之。

translations.literal: When bandits violated Wenzhou, Kekuan defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits struck Wenzhou, Kekuan defeated them.

sentences.zh: 其據昌國衛者，為大猷擊退。

translations.literal: Those occupying Changguo Guard were driven off by Dayou.
translations.idiomatic: Those at Changguo Guard were driven off by Dayou.

sentences.zh: 而賊首汪直復糾島倭及漳、泉群盜連巨艦百余蔽海至，濱海數千里同告警。

translations.literal: Bandit leader Wang Zhi again gathered island Japanese and Zhang and Quan pirates with more than a hundred great ships covering the sea; the coast for several thousand li was alarmed together.
translations.idiomatic: Leader Wang Zhi gathered island Japanese and pirates with more than a hundred great ships; thousands of li of coast were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 上海及南匯、吳淞、乍浦、蓁嶼諸所皆陷，蘇、松、寧、紹諸衛所州縣被焚掠者二十余。

translations.literal: Shanghai, Nanhui, Wusong, Zhapu, Qin Island, and more than twenty guards, posts, prefectures, and counties of Su, Song, Ning, and Shao were seized and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Shanghai, Nanhui, Wusong, and more than twenty prefectures and counties of Su, Song, Ning, and Shao were seized and burned.

sentences.zh: 留內地三月，飽而去。

translations.literal: They remained inland three months, sated, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They remained inland three months, sated, and departed.

sentences.zh: 忬乃言將士逐毀其船五十余艘。

translations.literal: Yu then said officers and soldiers had destroyed more than fifty of their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported officers and soldiers had destroyed more than fifty ships.

sentences.zh: 於是先所奪文武將吏俸，皆得復。

translations.literal: Thereupon the salaries of civil and military officials previously seized were all restored.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries of officials previously seized were restored.

sentences.zh: 尋以給事王國禎言，改巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon, on Supervising Secretary Wang Guozhen's word, he was changed to grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Wang Guozhen's recommendation, he became grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 忬方視師閩中，賊復大至，犯浙江，盧鏜等頻失利。

translations.literal: Yu was directing troops in Fujian when bandits came again in force, violating Zhejiang; Lu Zhen and others repeatedly suffered defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was directing troops in Fujian when bandits struck Zhejiang again; Lu Zhen suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 御史趙炳然劾其罪，帝特宥忬，忬因請築嘉善、崇德、桐鄉、德清、慈溪、奉化、象山城，而恤被寇諸府。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Bingran impeached his offenses; the emperor specially pardoned Yu, who requested building walls at Jiashan, Chongde, Tongxiang, Deqing, Cixi, Fenghua, and Xiangshan and relief for raided prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Bingran impeached him; the emperor pardoned Yu, who requested walls at seven counties and relief for raided prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時已遣尚書張經總督諸軍。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Jing had already been dispatched as grand coordinator of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Jing had been dispatched as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 大同適中寇，督撫蘇祐、侯鉞俱被逮，乃進忬右副都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: Datong was then hit by raiders and Grand Coordinators Su You and Hou Yue were both arrested; Yu was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Datong was raided and coordinators Su You and Hou Yue arrested; Yu was promoted to Grand Coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 秋防事竣，就加兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When autumn defense ended he was made Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn defense ended he was made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 薊遼總督楊博還朝，即移忬代之。

translations.literal: Yang Bo, grand coordinator of Ji and Liao, returned to court and Yu was moved to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo returned to court and Yu replaced him as Grand Coordinator of Ji and Liao.

sentences.zh: 尋進右都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 忬言：「騎兵利平地，步兵利險阻。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Cavalry excel on level ground; infantry excel in difficult terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: "Cavalry excel on level ground; infantry excel in difficult terrain.

sentences.zh: 今薊鎮畫地守，請去他郡防秋馬兵八千，易之以步，歲省銀五萬六千余兩。」

translations.literal: Now Ji garrison defends by demarcated territory; I request removing eight thousand autumn-defense cavalry horses from other prefectures and replacing them with infantry, saving more than fifty-six thousand taels yearly.
translations.idiomatic: I request removing eight thousand autumn-defense cavalry from other prefectures for infantry, saving fifty-six thousand taels yearly.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 打來孫十余萬騎深入廣寧諸處，總兵官殷尚質等戰歿。

translations.literal: Dalai Sun led more than a hundred thousand horsemen deep into Guangning; Regional Commander Yin Shangzhi and others died in battle.
